Arsenal fans must be thinking this is a job for the box-crasher himself, Mikel Merino.

Leeds squeeze Arsenal’s attack again and the ball runs out for a goalkick after Odegaard’s attempt to free White down the right fails.

No changes. Tanaka needs to be more discreet this half if he is to avoid a second yellow card. Arsenal attack quickly down the right buy Muharemovic sticks with Saka all the way to usher the ball out for a goalkick.

8 - Arsenal (5) and Leeds United (3) recorded eight offsides in total in the first half, the most in the opening 45 minutes of a Premier League game since Manchester United v Aston Villa in April 2023 (also 8). Lines. https://t.co/er4wTVAIJS

Arteta just wrote a few notes on the little notepad he keeps in his pocket. He has plenty to sort out during the break… Leeds have created the better chances here and Arsenal are looking short of ideas once they get into the opposition half. You can see why Farke’s side are undefeated so far this season.

Justin sweeps up for Leeds when Arsenal try to play head tennis on the Leeds box. Moments before Saka had ended up horizontally in the box when Muharemovic was shielding a long ball back to Trafford. The home crowd wants a penalty but no way.

Ally McCoist is ladling praise on Leeds’ organisation and discipline. And has special garlands for Calvert-Lewin who feels the referee is giving him nothing when manhandled by Konsa and Gabriel.

Three minutes of stoppage time are signalled, almost all for Justin’s splattered nose.

Arsenal were caught offside four times in the opening 16 minutes vs Leeds. That's 24 offsides in Premier League games for the season so far, which is at least twice as many as any every other team (Leeds, Brighton, Spurs 12 each) . https://t.co/jnTQah5bh4

Great save from Raya when Gudmundsson’s thumping volley on the end of Bogle’s superb, deep cross is blocked at the near post. Okafor set the move going with a fine crossfield pass.

Arsenal keep the ball but are being pushed back and forced to horseshoe from right to left wing. Madueke suddenly accelerates and drives towards the box to belt over a cross that havertz, from a very tight angle, heads miles over.

It feels like there’s 15 yellow shirts out there, which is testament to the organisation (and physical size?) of this Leeds team. They have been the better side. Tanaka and Stach are frustrating the Arsenal midfielders.

Two more Leeds names in the book: Ampadu for a late foul on Odegaard and Farke’s when the fourth official dobs him in to referee for something he said.

The crowd is growing frustrated by how well Leeds are playing and how little space they are allowing Arsenal.

Okafor overhits a pass in from the left that would have put Stach through on to the keeper. Then Tanaka is penalised for bodychecking Lewis-Skelly and goes into the book.

Oakfor rolls the ball into an empty net when Raya runs out but the whistle had already gone because Calafiori had triggered the trap perfectly.

Chances at both ends as Raya comes off his line, swats a punch to Amapdu who tries to loop it over him. Raya runs back to catch it and drifts very close to his goal-line. But he then instigates a counter with a brilliant pass out to the left and Madueke crosses fro Saka who is well held off by Muharemovic.

David Raya gets back to his line to keep out the looping header 🧤 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/53ilZvYwAY

It’s been a slow burner but the game is heating up now. That Leeds chance at the back post (Bogle accidentally blocking Stach’s volley) has sent a jolt of nervous electricity around the Emirates. Leeds are looking good at the back and increasingly dangerous in attack.

Ampadu wants to know why Saka isn’t being booked as he fouls Justin, a second foul in 30 seconds by the winger.

Justin is not allowed back on for far too long but eventually gets the nod as Tanaka refuses to be mesmerised by Saka’s footwork, watches the ball, nicks it off him and is tripped by the England winger when he tries to bomb off upfield after his tackle.

Justin affects the Blackadder ‘wibble’ look minus the Y-fronts on his head to continue. A bung up each nostril.

Trafford’s long free-kick is headed back to Raya.

Raya is fouled at the corner. Madueke whacks Justin across the ankles in an undetected foul and the Leeds defender faceplants into the turf and sits up with blood streaming out of his nose.

Another half chance for Leeds when Bogle pops up in the inside-left channel when a cross bypasses Calvert-Lewin. He tries to hook it over Konsa and blast it past Raya who spreads himself to turn it behind.

Good cross from Gudmundsson on the left dips perfectly for Stach to volley but Bogle can’t get out of the way. He is a prolific underlapper and pays the price here, blocking his team-mate’s shot.

Tanaka loses the ball in midfield and Arsenal pile forward but Leeds mass the ranks of their defence and block the path to goal until Justin is fouled to relieve the siege.

It’s the incisive, between-the-lines passes that Arsenal are currently lacking. Perhaps a bit of rustiness after such a long break between games?

Calafiori drives past Bogle and whips over a cross that is behind Havertz who has to backpedal to head it which robs his effort of power. Trafford drops to his knees to gather.

Rice takes an unnecessary touch instead of playing a first-time through ball to Madueke and Leeds recover to attack up the left. Okafor’s cross sails way too long and Bogle cannot keep it in.

Lewis-Skelly holds off Stach but then throws up his arms as if flapping a cape and clocks Stach in the face. Leeds are awarded a free-kick.

Excellent hold-up play by Calvert-Lewin is ruined by a shoddy Amapadu pass. Arsenal move it out to the right where Leeds enmesh White in the offside trap again. The crowd howls in frustration.

Someone seems to be banging a drum. Is this Selhurst Park? Okafor is penalised for grabbing Konsa’s shirt as he tried to spin the centre-back on halfway. Arsenal switch it to their left and Calafiori crashes into the box to cross. The ball deflects through the area and over the penalty spot but there’s no runner to meet it.

As TNT Sports points out, Leeds are trying to press Arsenal high but the positioning of Rice and Lewis-Skelly is much better than it was at Brighton.

Leeds’ offside trap has been functioning well and now Arsenal’s well-oiled one kicks in to catch Gudmundsson and Okafor.

Arsenal have been eager to play quick passes over the Leeds defence in these opening exchanges. Arteta’s side usually prefer to build up more slowly but they are looking for Havertz quite early. A consequence, perhaps, of Leeds pushing quite high up the pitch.

Okafor’s blistering 20-yard shot is deflected behind for a corner. The linesman’s flag was up because he said Calvert-Lewin had moved towards the ball in an offside position but the referee overrules him.

Arsenal defend the cross solidly but Bogle is covering diligently when they try to play Madueke clear with a long ball.

Now Madueke is caught offside on the left after a Muharemovic mistake threatened to let Havertz burst through before he laid it off instead.

Justin heads the ball to Ampadu who plays a one-two with Stach then chips the ball 40 yards, a real up and under, for Calvert-Lewin to chase. Raya beats him to it.

Aresnal launch a counter up the right and the telepathy between White and Saka for once breaks down when White runs offside for a return pass. Elvedi was there to sweep up in any case.

Muharemovic reads the game well and snuffs out a long pass looking for Havertz, shifts the ball up to Calvert-Lewin who is grabbed round the waist by Gabriel and Leeds are awarded a free-kick in the centre-circle.

Saka, miles offside, takes on a cross that he should have headed with a leaping volley instead and Trafford saves at very close range. Slick work between Odegaard and Madueke to get the ball to Saka.

Both sides used the opportunity of the playing of The Angel to muster in huddles. Leeds kick off, attacking from right to left, going all the way back to Trafford standing outside his box and he clips a long pass up the right and Leeds are immediately penalised with the linesman’s flag.

Arsenal switch to their right and try to free Saka but Trafford comes out to kick it into touch.

Arsenal in red and white, Leeds in yellow and black. Ben White was looking round to see if there was anyone in the Leeds line he recognised from his excellent year’s loan with them but Marcelo Bielsa’s promotion heroes have all moved on now. In fact, with Illan Meslier, there are two at the Gunners and none at Elland Road.

Long international break, we recovered most of our players and have a point to prove after our last game.

[Declan Rice] needed that [break] after everything he’s done over the years. He has looked fresh this week.

Everyone is fit and ready to play but we have a very difficult opponent.

We know that today is one of the toughest tasks in European football. They have been the most consistent side in Europe for years. Especially after a warning shot in the last game, they will be on it today.

But we didn’t win our good start in the lottery we earned it. We travel here in confidence.

Brighton didn’t park the bus. They went for it and pressed Arsenal. You need to do this. You have to go for it. If you sit deep their individual quality is too good. The one thing is to have a plan and a theory but another to execute it.

Last season we faced one of the best sides in the world so we didn’t dwell on [those defeats]. If we are at our best we have a chance to compete for points.

There’s no doubt who the biggest threat to Arsenal’s defence will be today: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has four goals in six games in all competitions this season and is the top scoring Englishman in the league since the start of last season. He’s a player Arsenal once looked at signing, many years ago.

Joe Cole is trying to make a case that Manchester City are not guilty of cheating because financial doping is not the same as taking drugs or match-fixing. A man who won all his medals at Abramovich’s Chelsea says it ‘is not right to class it as cheating’.

This is where punditry is broken. A former player may have an opinion on the subject of finance but it does not sound as though he is particularly informed and yet he’s given time to witter on because he doesn’t ‘feel’ it’s right.

"If they're found guilty, they have to lose those trophies that they won." 🏆 Martin Keown and Joe Cole debate whether Man City's recent trophies would be tainted if they're found guilty. 🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/TzrWkCQcI4

The most interesting aspect of that Arsenal lineup, I think, is the inclusion of Noni Madueke. It seems like he’ll be on the left flank, as the replacement for the injured Christos Tzolis. Madueke has played a handful of games on the left since joining Arsenal from Chelsea but it hasn’t happened nearly as frequently as had been expected when he first arrived. A left-footer on the left wing: old-school!

Leeds United Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Stach, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin.Substitutes Zetterer, Bard, Bijol, Gruev, Longstaff, Aaronson, Wilson, Bahoya, Nmecha.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

#1310. English soccer star gunned down outside Mississippi taco shop... months after moving to US to pursue his sporting dream

Published: 13:30 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 13:30 EST, 25 November 2026

An English soccer star has been killed outside a Mississippi taco restaurant just months after moving to the United States to chase his dreams.

Krissh Mahatma, 18, was fatally struck by a bullet after a gun was fired outside the Green Ghost Tacos restaurant in Jackson at around 3:39 a.m. on Sunday morning.

The London-born player was with teammates from his Co-Lin Wolves team when they came across a drunk man outside the restaurant, according to Dark Horse Press.

A fight broke out and a man pulled out a gun and fired into the group, hitting Mahatma, who was taken to a nearby hospital via a private vehicle where he died, according to Hinds County Coroner Jeramiah Howard, via WLBT.

Capitol Police have since arrested and charged Danny Luna, 22, with murder. The Mississippi Department of Public Safety did not elaborate on what caused the deadly confrontation.

'While this arrest is an important step toward justice, we recognize that nothing can ease the pain of losing a loved one,' Police Chief Mark Miller said, sending 'thoughts and prayers' to Mahatma's 'family and loved ones.'

Mahatma, who played as a striker, was in his freshman year at Copiah-Lincoln Community College in Wesson, around 45 miles south of Jackson where the incident took place.

Krissh Mahatma, 18, was fatally shot outside a taco restaurant in Jackson, Mississippi

Danny Luna, 22, has been arrested and charged with murder after the deadly confrontation

He had made 14 appearances in his first three months with the Co-Lin Wolves, scoring one goal in September in a 3-2 win over National Park College.

'Copiah-Lincoln Community College is mourning the loss of freshman soccer player Krissh Mahatma. Krissh will be deeply missed by his teammates and the entire Co-Lin family,' Dewayne Middleton, the Co-Lin president, said in a statement.

Before moving to the US, he had played for Watford 'A' in the post-16 Community and Education Football Alliance league. Co-Lin announced his signing in February.

A fundraiser set up to support his family said he was 'just beginning a new chapter of life far away from home' and added: 'his sudden passing has left his family, friends, teammates, coaches, and the entire Co-Lin soccer community heartbroken.

'Behind this tragedy is a family grieving the loss of their son and loved ones trying to make sense of a loss that feels impossible to put into words.'

The owner of the Green Ghost Tacos eatery said: 'On behalf of the entire Green Ghost family, I extend my deepest and most heartfelt condolences to the family, friends, loved ones, and university community mourning the tragic loss of a young student. Our hearts are heavy, and our thoughts and prayers are with everyone affected by this devastating incident.

'While this tragedy occurred near our establishment, we would like to clarify that Green Ghost was closed and was not conducting business at the time of the shooting.

'The safety and well-being of our patrons, employees, and surrounding community remain a top priority. We are committed to cooperating fully with law enforcement as they investigate the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident.

'Out of respect for the grieving family and the investigation, we will refrain from speculating or commenting further on the details at this time.

'Above all, we recognize that a family has suffered an unimaginable loss. We ask that the community join us in extending compassion, prayers, and support to those affected during this incredibly difficult time.'

#1309. Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

Schematic illustration and time-dependent HPLC analysis of oligomeric chain-extension products generated during CH3- and TETRA-initiated polymerization over 1–10 min. Stronger-binding CH3 produces a broader series of extension intermediates, whereas weaker-binding TETRA maintains a narrower chain-length distribution, consistent with more uniform chain growth during early propagation.

a, MST binding curves of natural HA oligomers (HA4–HA20) and non-natural initiators (HA-TETRA, TRI, GlcNAcβ-R (GlcNAcβ1-4GlcAβ1-3Galβ1-4Glc), GlcNAcα-R (GlcNAcα1-4GlcAβ1-3Galβ1-4Glc) and HA-TRI) with HAS. b, Corresponding dissociation constants (Kd), spanning the nanomolar to sub-millimolar range. c, NMR T2 relaxation analysis of the strongly binding initiators HA4 and HA6 and the more weakly binding HA-TETRA in the absence and presence of HAS. d, NMR T2 relaxation analysis of HA8, showing minimal T2 shortening upon HAS addition. e, Plots of Mn and Đ as a function of [M0]/[I0], for polymerization initiated by HA8. f, Comparison of Đ obtained with different initiators at [M0]/[I0] = 200. MST and NMR are presented as mean ± s.d. from technical replicate measurements (n = 3 or 4). The error bars in f indicate SEC analysis uncertainty.

For iMal4, the Đ value at [M0]/[I0] = 800 was used because of the low signal-to-noise ratio at [M0]/[I0] = 500. #1308. Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

The late chaos is over at Old Trafford as Solanke rescues a precious point for Tottenham with that 92nd minute equaliser. Man Utd thought they had the game wrapped up after Mbeumo’s well-taken opener was followed by Bentancur’s crazy red card. However, Spurs, who were the better team throughout the contest, kept fighting and found a fully deserved leveller. Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

Martinez lunges in on Maddison and brings down the playmaker with a foul. The centre-back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Baleba unleashes Mbeumo with an over-the-top through ball. Racing through on goal, the forward shoots, but from an unfavourable angle, Kinsky parries his near post effort out for a corner.

It’s all kicked off at Old Trafford! Bentancur flies in with a risky challenge on Shaw. The Man Utd defender is furious with the tackle and the two players square up to each other. Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

Van Hecke allows the forward to turn and Mbeumo slides a delightful effort into the far bottom corner. Old Trafford erupts in joy. Tottenham can’t believe it.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

That’s the question De Zerbi will be asking himself and his players at half-time...

Nothing to separate @ManUtd and @SpursOfficial at half-time... https://t.co/yJc8pvyfLl

There will be one minute of added time to round off this first half.

Spurs go close again! Solanke plays in Gallagher, who bundles his way into the six-yard box. Tielemans, Martinez and Yoro all fail to apprehend the Spurs midfielder, who digs a close-range shot out of his feet. However, Lammens is there to make a crucial block and thwart the visitors.

Spurs have been on top in this half but there has been a lack of quality from both teams. It has been a scrap between two average teams. Conor Gallagher the most influential player on the pitch so far.

Following Solanke and Kudus’ earlier chances, Spurs have been quiet going forward. Man Utd have been slowly growing into the game.

Amad is dribbling with intent and Gallagher bumps into him. The referee doesn’t give a free-kick and the home fans aren’t happy with that decision. It’s also worth remembering that Gallagher is on a yellow card. He needs to be careful.

Amad forces a save from Kinsky! Man Utd clear a Tottenham corner and burst forward on the counter through Mbeumo. The former Brentford man is chased by Tonali and has Amad in support, before playing the pass into the 24-year-old. Udogie closes down the angle, forcing Amad to take the chance with a first-time shot. His fizzing strike is comfortably collected by Kinsky, but that is more encouraging from the hosts.

You can feel the nervousness in the Old Trafford crowd. Spurs’ dominance has calmed over the last 10 minutes, but Man Utd have failed to take control or pick up the tempo.

This game looks it could be time for Baleba’s much-anticipated debut. Man Utd’s current midfield doesn’t possess enough running power and Tottenham are exploiting that.

Man Utd’s slow start prompts some boos from the home fans. Cunha attempts to rally the crowd, but his side have given their supporters nothing to be positive about in this game so far. From a Spurs perspective, you can see why they’ve only scored two top-flights goals this season. They should be two-nil up, but they’ve notably lacked end-product.

Tottenham miss another golden chance! It’s a brilliant passing move from defence to attack. It ends with Savio teeing up Kudus with an intelligent cross. The Ghanaian can’t quite fully wrap his foot around the delivery, and from inside the penalty area, he slams an unmarked effort wide of the bottom corner.

Currently, Man Utd are being outnumbered in midfield. The interchangeability of Tonali, Bergvall and Gallagher is running rings around Mainoo and Tielemans. Fernandes’ lack of defensive instinct is leaving the hosts’ midfield pivot exposed.

Man Utd then make a rare foray forward as Cunha whips in a cross towards Amad. Udogie is alert to the danger and gets in front of the winger to clear.

Ex-Nottingham Forest manager Steve Cooper is here in the directors’ box at Old Trafford. He was last at Brondby in Denmark and will inevitably be considered for jobs here in England as chairmen look to make changes during the season.

Still, it’s Tottenham forcing the issue as Kudus dashes past Shaw with his blistering pace. Cunha tracks back but can’t stop the winger from digging out a cross. Yoro’s skewed clearance is headed back to Lammens by Tielemans. Man Utd need to careful, they cannot continue playing like this.

The visitors then steam forward again on the counter. On this occasion, Yoro defends magnificently, executing a well-timed sliding tackle on Van Hecke.

The visitors have made an excellent start to this game. Savio breezes past Maguire like he isn’t even there, but can’t quite find Kudus with his low cross. De Zerbi will want his side to capitalise on this dominant period. Man Utd look sluggish and asleep so far.

Gallagher receives an early yellow card after pulling Maguire back. Referee Attwell isn’t taking any prisoners. Man Utd supporters also show their love and appreciation for Rui Pinto with this banner.

Tottenham waste a huge chance! What is Lammens doing?! The Man Utd goalkeeper tries to pick out Mainoo with a very risky pass. It’s intercepted by Bergvall, who tees up Solanke. One-on-one with Lammens, the Spurs striker’s whipped effort is blocked by Lammens. The Belgian goes from zero to hero, emphatically redeeming himself.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Can either of these sides pick up a victory to relieve the pressure on their head coach?

“You cheating b******s, you know what you are,” is heard from the stands at Old Trafford. It’s pretty safe to say they are referring to Manchester City’s guilty verdict which was announced during the international break.

Man Utd, skippered by Fernandes, receive a feverish reception as they’re welcomed onto the pitch by the Old Trafford faithful. Tottenham are led out by Solanke, who captains the visitors today.

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Our Spurs side to face Man Utd 🫡 🔢 @krakenfx https://t.co/jZOhKEUoYc

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

The spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after big-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1307. Furious Premier League refs 'SHOCKED' at Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool being overturned: Row erupts over Man United star's ban being scrapped… despite key panel voting unanimously that decision was RIGHT

Published: 14:56 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 25 November 2026

Premier League officials are 'shocked and furious' after the FA overturned Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool - despite the competition's own independent panel unanimously backing the dismissal.

Daily Mail Sport understands that the Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel has returned a 5-0 verdict in support of referee Sam Barrott's decision to send off Yoro. The panel also backed VAR's decision not to intervene. Their findings will be released next Wednesday.

But an extraordinary row has now erupted, with United celebrating a successful appeal while the Premier League and refereeing body Pro Ref stand by the original decision.

United appealed against the red card following Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield - Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge - and an independent FA regulatory commission, consisting of three former players, rescinded Yoro's one-match ban on Tuesday.

The Frenchman was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he ran clear on goal in the eighth minute. United disputed the referee's view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, having taken a heavy touch.

The FA panel appeared to agree, on the basis Yoro did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity, meaning the Frenchman is free to play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Referee Sam Barrott showed Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card vs Liverpool

Yoro was sent off for this foul on Alexander Isak - but his red card was overturned on Tuesday

Barrott and his on-field officiating team from Sunday are believed to be angry at the overturn

However, top-flight officials are now understood to be demanding answers as to how this has happened, with Pro Ref chief Howard Webb backing his referees.

'That (the red card) was the referee's call, made on the field,' said Webb. 'Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect - and formed the opinion it wasn't.

'I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.'

United sources have branded this interpretation as 'totally wrong' and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott's decision.

United dispute that it was a subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

The Premier League and Pro Ref did not comment.

#1306. The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

“It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”

Maresca said City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

“The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he said. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”

The Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

“The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”

News breaks that City had been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.

Telegraph Sport understands that Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur were contacted in advance of the email to the other 15 clubs.

In a letter to fans, a defiant Khaldoon Al Mubarak, City’s chairman, expresses complete confidence that his club would be vindicated.

“There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our club,” he writes. “We will not give them that opportunity.”

With the football world still making sense of the news, Tony Pulis admits to feeling “cheated”. His Stoke City side were defeated by Manchester City in the 2011 FA Cup final, during the 2009-23 period.

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali then likens City’s transgressions to “doping” before Mauricio Pochettino, whose Spurs side were often in the hunt with City for major trophies during his time as manager, says that football has “lived through a period of deception”.

The Premier League reveals that City’s owners inflated “sham” sponsorship deals by £830.69m between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

It also discloses that image rights had been inflated and key witnesses had lied.

Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group, appears helpless when questioned about the verdict’s findings at the European Football Clubs’ general assembly in Copenhagen by Sky News.

An unblinking Soriano then features in a video statement published by City in which he claimed their guilty verdict was based on “a single false accusation”.

With City on the ropes, Pep Guardiola releases a statement in support of his former club, assuring supporters that “we will get through this together”.

The Prime Minister says that he would be “really concerned” to lose City’s owners, but after significant backlash, No 10 moves to clarify his reaction saying that “if wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences”.

It later amends the statement to “wherever wrongdoing is established”.

The UAE then warns Andy Burnham that it will pull billions of pounds of investment out of the UK in retaliation for the guilty verdict against City.

City argue that their sponsorship deals were part-funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, in their appeal, which claims bank statements and witness accounts provide “irrefutable evidence” to support their case.

Liverpool arrive at their team hotel for their game against Manchester City! https://t.co/M8CizGPQXg

😤 "They're about to find out how angry every other club is." 🗣️ Alan Shearer shares his thoughts on the Man City charges. https://t.co/9Oby6XT60j

The Liverpool head coach was asked for his reaction to City’s guilty verdict in his pre-match press conference and, as with many of his peers, he kept his response brief.

“Uncertainty is not good for anyone involved,” he said. “But there is the process ongoing and we have to be patient like everyone else and see what happens at the end.”

It is the most unlikely Oasis song title for a banner but, in a sea of canvas, the word will jump out from the Kop: Acquiesce.

The simplest flags frequently carry the most profound messages and, on a red background, below Acquiesce is the declaration: “MCFC Cheats”. It has been prepared specially and specifically for the return of domestic football to Anfield.

Given the tone coming out of the Etihad Stadium, nobody will be acquiescing to any alleged wrongdoing, certainly not on Sunday, but minds were made up on Merseyside about how far City had pushed the boundaries in pursuit of success a long time ago.

“There has been a lot of talk about various things,” explains John Gibbons, host of Anfield Wrap, the popular Liverpool podcast. “Manchester City trying to say they are going to be hard done to, but there are no great surprises among Liverpool fans about these charges, are there?

“Everyone who goes to the match, who supports Liverpool, have known all along that a lot of those sponsorship deals looked questionable. Did they pass the smell test? That’s why the atmospheres in the past when City came were always brilliant and I’m expecting it will be the same again.”

So that is why Anfield will be a maelstrom of sound and fury for one of the most significant occasions in Premier League history.

The half-and-half scarves have been replaced by more topical match-day merchandise this afternoon...

Here is what City’s head coach said during his first press conference after the guilty verdict:

“There is a process ongoing and in this moment I completely trust the club … I trust the club because I trust the people and this is also the reason why I joined the club. And then there is not another club in the world where I would [rather] be.”

“Absolutely not. The last time I was here was the treble season. I know the effort from the players, from the club, from the manager in that time that was Pep [Guardiola]. I know exactly the effort that the club put to achieve that kind of target.”

“I won the Championship with Leicester. League One, we will see, but we are thinking about something that we don’t know.”

I’m not worried at all. The environment [among] the players is nice. In this moment we are top of the league so the players have all the reason to be happy and excited.

“One hundred per cent… Because I know the organisation from years ago, and I know how serious they are, I know that they do the right things. I would like to speak about this when we win the appeal.”

While Liverpool have struggled for wins in this fixture of late, it’s worth noting that this run includes five draws.

Liverpool have won just three of their last 13 Premier League clashes with Man City 👀 https://t.co/OxkeDpLjQq

On Saturday Manchester United fans resurrected their “ticker” mocking Manchester City’s trophy drought following their rivals’ cheating scandal:

There was also a nod to Rui Pinto, the whistleblower whose Football Leaks documents prompted the Premier League’s investigation into City:

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

“We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission said. I think that’s what’s worried me.”

"Enjoy the ride and smile" Erling Haaland with a message for Man City fans ahead of their trip to Anfield this weekend 🎙️🩵 https://t.co/H7so0fk6XE

“The international break is good because we can review what we have done and what we can do better,” Enzo Maresca said after Manchester City’s harum-scarum 5-3 victory over Sunderland. “But at the same time we can relax a little bit more.” One wonders how much respite Enzo Maresca and Manchester City actually enjoyed in the intervening 21 days.

Since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca said, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

#1305. OUT OF THIS WORLD! Celtic link up with data analytics firm Pluto to improve recruitment

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:52 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 18:32 EST, 25 November 2026

Celtic have announced a long-term partnership with a company the club believe will transform their recruitment.

London-based Pluto Data Analytics use predictive analytics and AI to help football clubs with player identification. The initial deal lasts three years, with scope for extension.

Celtic believe the deal will ‘support the club’s continuing commitment to innovation and excellence in football operations by enhancing recruitment analysis, talent identification, squad planning and broader football decision-making processes.’

The Parkhead club’s recruitment strategy has been heavily criticised by supporters in recent seasons amid their struggles in Europe and increased domestic competition from Rangers and Hearts.

A statement explaining the arrangement added: ‘The partnership forms part of Celtic’s ongoing investment in modern football infrastructure and its commitment to ensuring that football decisions are informed by the best available intelligence and expertise.

‘By working with Pluto Data Analytics, Celtic will gain access to enhanced analytical tools and insights to support its existing recruitment and football operations functions.

The Parkhead club are hoping that new deal will improve their recruitment process

‘The objective is clear: to improve decision-making, identify emerging opportunities and support the club’s long-term football strategy.’

The move comes following long-standing criticism that the Scottish champions’ means of scouting undervalued talents had become outdated, with their failure to act swiftly and efficiently in the transfer market leading to repeated failures in the European qualification rounds.

Rival clubs such as Hearts have benefited from the use of data thanks to the access they have had to Jamestown Analytics.

‘We are always looking for ways to strengthen our football operation and ensure that we continue to evolve in an increasingly competitive environment,’ said Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson.

‘We have been reviewing the options in this area in order to select the optimum model for our club.

‘Our partnership with Pluto Data Analytics, an organisation with real quality and pedigree within this field, reflects our commitment to innovation and continuous improvement.

O'Neill says he hopes partnership 'will help us deliver the success we are all striving for'

‘Recruitment remains one of the most important areas of any football club. Our aim is to identify talent as effectively as possible, reduce uncertainty where we can and support our football staff with the best available information.

‘We believe this partnership will strengthen our ability to support the club’s ambitions both domestically and in European competition.’

Manager Martin O’Neill added: ‘I am very pleased that Celtic and Pluto are joining together to give the club an extra level of insight and analysis which is becoming more prominent in football.

‘While football is not an exact science, if the club can access and utilise new tools and new details, ultimately, we hope that such data will help us deliver the success we are all striving for.

Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson says Pluto deal is 'optimum model' for the club

‘Our recruitment and wider football operations teams have already engaged with Pluto. Our plans in the short, medium and longer term are being developed and we are confident that our relationship will deliver real tangible benefit to the club over the next few years.’

Jon Godfrey, CEO of Pluto Data Analytics, said: ‘Today is a big day for Pluto and we are incredibly excited to be working with Celtic, one of the biggest clubs in world football.

‘We believe that predictive data modelling combined with the allure and resources of such a famous institution will allow us to achieve great things in this partnership.

‘Celtic has the capacity to compete at the highest levels of European football and it is an honour and a fantastic challenge to work relentlessly with the club on achieving the exciting goals we have put in place.’

#1304. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Coventry City  Rushworth; Van Ewijk, Pinnock, Thomas, Dasilva; Yirenkyi, Grimes; Thomas-Asante, Rudoni, Mason-Clark; Cherif. Substitutes Bentley, Sakamoto, Simms, Mfuni, Onyeka, Latibeaudiere, Torp, Gboho, Hamer.

Only the one change for the Toon, Nico González in for Steur. But just look at that bench where Burn, Dedic, Osula and Joelinton are all welcomed back.

Frank Lampard AKA Frankie Lampart Junior (admittedly 29 years ago) has made two changes, Cherif replacing Onyeka and Van Ewijk, back from injury, for Mfuni. Seems to be reverting to a back four too:

City for Newcastle tonight. 📋 https://t.co/GDk4xXhqST

Advertisement | GambleAware | 18+ Betting on the football tonight? Take a look at these tips and offers chosen by Telegraph Media Group

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#1303. Liverpool fans are enjoying watching their team again as they close in on Champions League qualification after Club Brugge victory... now it's time for Andoni Iraola to make it a perfect week at Everton, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 17:09 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 18:48 EST, 25 November 2026

Andoni Iraola tried to stifle a smirk on Tuesday when it was put to him that he had a fair chance of completing a perfect week by thrashing Manchester United, winning away in Europe and then winning his first-ever Merseyside Derby.

The usual responses came back of remaining level-headed and not getting carried away, of course – but Iraola has ticked off two of those three tasks and now goes to Everton with his much-criticised, big-money signings in the form of their Liverpool careers.

That is Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, of course, who both scored here to further quash any narratives over them being expensive flops, a debate which had followed them for much of their first year or so on Merseyside.

Isak scored a brace to take his season tally to double-figures and make it six away games in a row where he has struck, while Wirtz followed up his best performance of the season against United with a fine strike from distance.

Wirtz especially has never been far away from criticism during his time at the club but is silencing his doubters every week and said this week that Iraola had helped him rediscover the player Liverpool thought they were buying for £116million two summers ago.

The sentiment spreads beyond Wirtz. After a season of strife, Iraola has brought the feel-good factor back at Anfield and supporters are enjoying watching their team again after a year in which it felt like a chore to do so some weeks.

Alexander Isak scored twice as Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League

That made it three wins in a row for the Reds as they start to really click under Andoni Iraola

CLUB BRUGGE (4-3-3): Sommer 4; Sabbe 5 (Siquet 84), Spileers 5, Mechele 6, Seys 6; Vetlesen 6 (Vermant 75), Potts 7 (Tsawa 84), Vanaken 6; Forbs 7, Tresoldi 6, Lemarechal 7 (Diakhon 75).

Subs not used: Jackers, Vanden Driessche, Han-beom Lee, Virgili, Dams, Robberechts, Audoor, Vasovic.

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 7; Frimpong 6 (Van Dijk 73, 6), Araujo 6, Jacquet 7, Kerkez 6; Nyoni 7 (Mac Allister 73, 6), Szoboszlai 7; Munoz 6 (Ngumoha 42, 6), Wirtz 7, Barcola 6 (Chambers 86); ISAK 8 (Koumas 86).

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Tsimikas, McConnell, Danns.

It is making the Liverpool fans fall for Iraola a little bit more each week. How that feeling would be turbocharged with Derby delight at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday.

‘I was very pleased with the result and the performance overall,’ said Iraola. ‘At 3-0, you can think it was an easy game and I don’t think it was. We were facing a really good team.’

As the 1,000 or so travelling Kop enjoyed their strong Belgian beers and chocolate waffles in this quaint, picturesque city, they were still laughing about poor old Manchester United and Sunday’s 4-0 demolition job.

This was a much tougher test against an opposition that had started well in the Champions League with three wins from four, so Liverpool’s performance was never going to be as convincing – but the victory was still important.

It helped them take a step closer to cementing a top eight place in this long-winded league phase. That would ease the pressure on a congested calendar by seeing them not only be able to rest players in the latter games of the league stage but also skip a play-off round.

Club Brugge are no mugs and they showed that, with energetic winger Carlos Forbs the pick of the bunch. The former Manchester City academy starlet has inherited a certain Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt at Portugal and gave Milos Kerkez a testing night here.

The Belgian side, like Liverpool, had won three of their first four European games including victory away to Inter. They had won five of the last seven league titles with a brave playing style that Iraola admitted was a pleasure to analyse – which he added was not always the case.

Their bold approach was their undoing here, though, with possession tossed away far too easily for Liverpool’s opener after 13 minutes. Yann Sommer, in the winter of his career at 37, passed straight to Bradley Barcola who, via stand-in skipper Dominik Szoboszlai, found Isak.

The Swede needed no second invitation to fire home his ninth goal of the season. Isak had been rested for most of Liverpool’s early European outings but was the difference here and loves playing away: he has now netted on his last six games away from Anfield.

Liverpool have 12 points from five games and will almost certainly be in the knockout stages

Florian Wirtz continued his fine form as he curled in a delightful effort to put Liverpool 2-0 up

Iraola will hope to make it the perfect week with victory in Sunday's Merseyside Derby

Only Mohamed Salah has done so in seven or more in recent history for Liverpool. Everton would be a fine place to match that record.

Despite the scoreline flattering Liverpool, things were far from easy after Isak’s opener. Alisson was needed to deny Felix Lemarechal both sides at half-time and Virgil van Dijk – rested from the start – was called on as a second-half substitute to steady the ship.

Winger Victor Munoz limped off in agony after going down before half-time holding his knee. Iraola feared the worst when a stretcher was called but the Spaniard walked off and was feeling ‘optimistic’ after the match, according to the boss.

Szoboszlai should have put the game to bed after a sublime team move led to the Hungarian being thwarted by Sommer at point-blank range, while Barcola was also guilty of wastefulness after getting his feet tangled up when in a dangerous position.

But Wirtz, in the best form of his Liverpool career, made it three goals in his last three with a fine strike from distance that clipped in off the post.

Then Isak raced through on goal and dinked a shot over Sommer for goal No 10 of the season for him. It completed a memorable night for Iraola and his big-money boys. Now to make it a perfect week at Everton on Sunday.

#1302. Augmenting reality with integrated photonics

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature volume 659, pages 915–926 (2026) Cite this article

Augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally new ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.
