#1277. Senne Lammens has NOT fully recovered from World Cup howler, claims Peter Schmeichel after Man United goalkeeper's nightmare in Lisbon - as Joshua Zirkzee insists squad will rally around under-fire team-mate

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER

Published: 04:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 06:54 EST, 26 November 2026

Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel fears Senne Lammens has yet to recover from the blunder he made during Belgium's World Cup campaign last summer.

Lammens made two costly mistakes in United’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night, conceding a needless penalty and dropping a clanger in the dying minutes to allow Luis Suarez to score twice for the home side.

The 24-year-old goalkeeper, who was one of Manchester United's standout performers last season following his £18.1million transfer from Royal Antwerp, has looked unconvincing so far this term and played a part in the club conceding more goals (35) than any other side in Europe's top five leagues.

Former Red Devils goalkeeper Schmeichel believes Lammens has never fully recovered from his error that led to Belgium being dumped out by Spain at the World Cup quarter-final stage last summer.

In the 88th minute of the match, with the score locked at 1-1, Lammens spilled the ball into the path of Mikel Merino, who tapped home to send Spain through to the semi-finals.

Asked if the confidence-shot goalkeeper should now be dropped by Mauricio Pochettino for Karl Darlow, who was signed by United in the summer, Schmeichel told CBS Sports: ‘I don’t know where that point is.

Senne Lammens made two big errors during Manchester United's 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon

Peter Schmeichel fears Lammens has never fully recovered from his blunder at the World Cup

‘Mauricio Pochettino has come in, he’s brought his own staff, that means he’s got a new goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him.

‘I don’t know if you remember in the World Cup, he came against Spain and made a bit of a mistake, Merino scored and they got knocked out, and I feel like he’s lost a little bit of confidence from that mistake, hasn’t really recovered.

‘As a goalkeeper when you’re not on your best form you need your defenders in front of you to help you out and the sad truth is that they haven’t been able to do that and of course, that makes it so much worse.'

Joshua Zirkzee insists United’s players will rally around Lammens and won’t let their under-fire goalkeeper ‘suffer by himself’.

The two costly errors undid Lammens’ good work after he saved an earlier penalty from Suarez, but Zirkzee said the players are determined to support the Belgian.

‘This team is a family, so there's no one who will suffer by themselves,’ said Zirkzee. ‘Mistakes happen. Let's go on to the next one. Senne’s a great goalkeeper.

‘In this moment, we just give him space. I’m not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne’s a great kid. He's got a good head on him and we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game. We didn't draw because of him. I'm also someone who likes to look at myself and, you know, I didn't score.’

United had two goals disallowed by Polish referee Szymon Marciniak as well as conceding the two penalties and seeing Youri Tielemans sent off – three days after Leny Yoro was shown a controversial red card at Liverpool – and Zirkzee admitted that it feels like the world is against Pochettino’s team at the moment.

The Belgian shot-stopper conceded a needless penalty just minutes after saving a spot-kick

He then spilled the ball into the path of Luis Suarez late on, gifting Sporting a late equaliser

‘Yeah, we're in a place where it can feel like that pretty quick,’ he added. ‘But as I said, we've got a locker-room that's built on supporting each other and we will get out of it eventually. If it's us against the world, so be it.

‘For the team that we are, we shouldn't really be looking at what the referee decides, but you cannot deny that it was some key decisions that weren't in our favour, to put it like that.

‘But, as I said, we shouldn't really be looking at the referee. All we have to do is look at ourselves. In the end, I think we drew because of small details, little mistakes. But we definitely have something to build on, mainly the way we started the second half. I think that's something we can build on and move on with. Our team should be capable to win even if we're not being favoured in those moments.’

#1273. 'We have players who have been here for four years and can't speak English': Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner slams stars for failing to adapt in England in press conference rant

Published: 04:12 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 07:31 EST, 26 November 2026

Oliver Glasner has criticised Nottingham Forest players that cannot speak English after being in the country for several years, as he called for higher standards at the club.

Forest are currently outside the Premier League relegation zone on goal difference after 11 matches, having won just twice in the top flight since Glasner's arrival in the summer.

Speaking ahead of their Friday night clash against Chelsea, Glasner highlighted the failure of some of his squad to learn English to illustrate how standards needed to rise at the club.

'Stability in a company is having standards,' Glasner said. 'Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough.

'We have players who are here for four years, can't speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language.

'For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English. If I want to manage in Italy, I have to speak Italian.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner has criticised stars for failing to speak English years after joining the club

Glasner highlighted the issue as an example as he insisted standards need to rise at the club

'Otherwise, Oliver Glasner, if you want to speak in your dialect, stay at home in Austria, everybody understands you, but nowhere else.'

Football clubs regularly enlist the services of language experts in an effort to help foreign stars to settle and communicate with their team-mates.

West Brom and Wolves have worked with Language Partners for around 20 years, with the company providing tailored classes to players and coaches, offering specific skills required for their role at the clubs.

Another company, Communicate Well, has worked with Premier League clubs since 1999, with lessons taking place at training grounds, players’ homes and ‘out and about’ to provide real-life tasks in English.

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez previously revealed Arsenal had included a £20,000 bonus in his first contract with the club, which would be paid when he passed the English proficiency test.

Martinez, who signed for Arsenal in the summer of 2010 from Argentine side Independiente, had reportedly passed the test before Christmas.

English stars moving abroad have received praise in recent years for their efforts to learn the native language, with Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Trent Alexander-Arnold having all made efforts to become fluent in Spanish.

Alexander-Arnold revealed he had worked with a Spanish tutor for five months prior to joining Real Madrid. The tutor revealed he had started ‘from zero’ but worked every day to be able to speak Spanish at his unveiling at the club.

After speaking Spanish at his Barcelona unveiling, Gordon explained he had initially begun learning the language at Everton when working under Rafael Benitez. He later spoke Spanish with a physio at Newcastle as he targeted a move to Barcelona, while the winger also underwent six formal lessons.

Joao Gomes is among Wolves' foreign imports to have worked with a specialist language company to help them settle at the club

Arsenal put a bonus in Emiliano Martinez's contract to encourage him to learn English

Trent Alexander-Arnold worked with a Spanish tutor for five months before his move to Real Madrid

Daily Mail Sport reported last month that Glasner had not been happy with some of his players' attitudes and their response to his work since joining the club from Crystal Palace in the summer.

Glasner had explosively hit out at his players after their 2-0 defeat at Brentford at the end of October, with the Austrian having warned players either had to buy into his methods to see a turnaround in form or they would have a sixth manager since the start of last season.

The 52-year-old's warning appeared to have been met with a positive response as Forest earned a stunning 3-1 victory over Man City before the international break, but they returned with a 2-0 loss at Bournemouth last weekend.

Glasner had maintained that his squad will have to work hard and show commitment both on and off the pitch to improve.

'We always try to support the players to get the best version of themselves that they can be. But at the end, the players that have to do it, they have to buy in, they have to listen and work hard on the pitch,' Glasner said.

'There is no other opportunity to improve, it would be easy laying on the sofa and doing nothing and you become a better football player or suddenly speak a language all of a sudden.

'It just doesn't work. It is all about how hard you work and how committed you are.

Glasner has insisted his squad need to work hard and show commitment to improve

'I believe none of our players have reached his personal ceilings so far, there is always bits to improve – physically, mentally, technically, tactically – there is always space to improve.

'The most important thing is that players want to improve, then it can happen.'

Glasner met with Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis in London earlier this week, where plans for the January transfer window were discussed.

Forest are expected to target adding around five players to their squad in the window as they bid to turn around their fortunes.

'He was asking "what do you need, what do you want here to improve in the squad, the staff and the environment",' Glasner said.

'He wants the best for Nottingham Forest, he wants the best for everyone here.

'We need to improve in the squad, in the staff, in the environment and this is our discussion. It was a fantastic meeting and it was worth spending six hours travelling.'

Forest face a Chelsea side on Friday that have lost three of their last four league matches.

Glasner’s side will then begin December with matches against Hull, Brighton and Sunderland as they bid to climb the table.

#1272. Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he said. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

“Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

“The first work to do is on me,” he said. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

“It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”

For all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage said. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”

Sage joined Palace after a fine campaign with Lens. He led the club to second place in Ligue 1, just six points off Paris St-Germain, and victory in the Coupe de France. Yet, despite Sage’s reputation when he moved to Selhurst Park, his suitability for the Palace job is increasingly being questioned.

Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Sage could suffer the same fate, with doubts growing that he will still be in charge for Thursday’s trip to Besiktas.

“It’s not my decision,” Sage said. “I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we are able to do better. And today the work is really important to do, and I will do it. It’s my job, and I’d like to change this.”

With only Manchester City and Arsenal above them, Brighton and Hove Albion are entitled to dream of making history. Yet, whatever happens between now and May, one accolade is already surely their own: the goal of the season award.

Diego Gómez’s 56-yard strike will instantly become the stuff of Brighton lore. The Paraguayan’s audacity will be even more cherished for coming against Crystal Palace, who were pummelled 5-0 in the M23 derby.

All Premier League defeats are equal but some are more equal than others. Three years ago, Patrick Vieira lost his job after a defeat by Brighton. Now, Pierre Sage is at grave risk of suffering the same fate. Naturally, Brighton fans revelled in reminding him of this threat as the final whistle approached.Palace were so ragged that their performance felt like a defeat that marks the end of a managerial reign. Even stand-in captain Adam Wharton was guilty of dawdling and losing the ball in possession. Hundreds of away supporters left well before the full-time whistle and those who remained booed all players bar Jefferson Lerma.

With less venom in attack, especially with Ismaïla Sarr being an unused substitute, Palace’s sole chance lay in counter-attacking. This strategy disintegrated in the fourth minute, when Jaydee Canvot headed Pascal Gross’s free-kick into his own net.

But the hint of self-immolation in Palace’s display should not obscure the swagger of Brighton’s performance. Despite losing Danny Welbeck, last year’s top scorer, Brighton have scored 23 goals already this Premier League campaign, the most in the league. This tally includes one of the most extraordinary goals in Premier League history.

Most simply, Gómez’s goal, which put Brighton 2-0 up in the seventh minute, was a triumph of the imagination. Receiving a short pass from Olivier Boscagli just inside his own half, Gómez could have sought to pick out a team-mate. Instead, his scanning of the pitch before receiving the ball had revealed that goalkeeper Walter Benítez was off his line and Brighton’s attacking players were being tightly guarded by defenders. It’s remarkable how easily Brighton are finding space between the lines, they’re pulling Palace’s markers to and fro, into and out of position.

Richards does get another go at tossing another throw-in back into the box, this time from the right, and Khalaili gets to this one, but heads well over.

Brighton utterly in control. They are dominating the ball and playing in a very controlled way, then bursting into life when Palace advance themselves.

Gomez has been fantastic this afternoon and he tiptoes his way past several Palace midfielders along the halfway line. Boscagli then has the presence of mind to switch the ball back out to the right and Gross’ set into the path of Kadioglu is struck goalwards and tipped behind by Benitez.

For the first time this afternoon, Mitchell makes a meaningful foray forward. He earns a throw-in near the corner flag which Richards launches into the box, but the ball slips out of his hands and Brighton clear their lines.

The resulting corner lands to Gross off the second phase but he cannot keep his effort down. He spins on his heels in frustration.

The hosts are letting Palace have the ball, settling into their defensive structure and funnelling the visitors around the outside, using the touchline as an extra defender to force errors.

Kadiologu works the ball infield from the right but cannot pick out Kostoulas. De Cuyper works the ball back into the middle for Ayari to strike goalwards from just outside the box, his effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

It’s taken Gross 30 minutes to make his first misstep. He goes into the book for a desperate tackle on Pino who had taken the ball away from the German with a superb first touch.

Close! A raking crossfield pass to Gomez at the far post is put back across the face of goal and a prone Ahanor is just about able to clear his lines. The young defender knew very little about that.

Brighton have complete control of the central areas, with Wharton and Timber struggling to get on top of their web of rotations and diversionary runs.

Palace win a free-kick 25 yards out and Pino, who has two goals in his last two outings, tries his luck but cannot clear the wall.

Brighton waste no time getting up the pitch and Kostoulas has a go from outside the box. His effort is straight at Benitez who gathers the ball at the second time of asking.

Danso is shown a red card as things go bad to worse for Sunderland at the Vitality. He brought down Evanilson as the Brazilian looked to be through on goal.

Finally some respite for Palace as Brighton choose to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure.

But back come the hosts soon after, De Cuyper bursting into the left of the box. This time Benitez is wise to the move and gets out smartly to cut it out.

Chants of “Are you Arsenal in disguise” ring out around the Amex...

This is utterly surreal. Gómez’s incredible strike had barely sunk in when Brighton harassed Palace again. This was a sumptuous team strike: a back heel from Kostoulas on the right setting up Ayari to tuck home. The atmosphere at Amex is electric. Brighton are heading second, below only Manchester City.

Brighton 3 Crystal Palace 0 (Gomez) Wow. Brighton are in dreamland here. Kostoulas finds space down the right and picks out the onrushing Ayari, whose effort beats Benitez via a Canvot deflection. That’s three goals in the first 10 minutes.

"Crystal Palace blown away here!" Brighton score a THIRD inside 10 minutes 🔥 https://t.co/YyoIw1zyaJ

Brighton 2 Crystal Palace 0 (Gomez) My goodness... That’s a goal-of-the-season contender, surely?! Wharton cedes possession on the halfway line and Gomez does the rest. He’s at most a yard inside Palace’s half and, spotting Benitez off his line, tries his luck from distance and finds the back of the net!

Goal of the season? From the halfway line, Diego Gómez picks up a loose ball and lobs Walter Benítez: shades of David Beckham at Wimbledon 30 years ago. Palace are in disarray.

"Would you look at that!" DIEGO GOMEZ SCORES FROM THE HALFWAY LINE! 🤯 https://t.co/qmagVbGEb4

Bournemouth 1 Sunderland 0 (Tavernier) A routine ball through the middle by Christie is not dealt with as Evanilson escapes the clutches of two defenders before squaring to Tavernier to finish.

Marcus Tavernier heads home his fourth goal of the season! 🍒 https://t.co/CI2pPjFw3I

Brighton 1 Crystal Palace 0 (Canvot OG) That’s superb from Gross. The German spins a delightful free-kick from the far side into the six-yard box and a retreating Canvot heads past his own goalkeeper.

Brighton only need three-and-a-half minutes to get their opener: a Pascal Gross free-kick from the left-hand side, headed into his own net by Palace centre-half Jaydee Canvot. Just the tonic for the thousands of Brighton fans being soaked.

Jaydee Canvot glances the ball into his own net and Brighton lead! 🔵 https://t.co/subm9ggwId

Kadioglu sets the tone early on, snapping in to cut off a loose pass out from the back by Palace. The ball is eventually worked up to Kostoulas, but he cannot bring it under his spell.

The heavens have opened up at the Amex, but that has not dampened the stadium announcer’s enthusiasm. He announces each player to the fans, with Pascal “the Goat” Gross’ name receiving an especially hearty cheer from the crowd.

The players (all 22 starters, it seems) take a knee before Brighton get us started.

The clouds have come in and the rain has started at the Amex as kick-off approaches. A raucous atmosphere, as you’d expect for the M23 derby, with plenty of Brighton fans relishing singing anti-Crystal Palace songs on the way to the ground. Should Brighton win - as they will expect to - they will move second, at least until Arsenal play later.

Kick-off is almost upon us. There’s just about enough time to make a brew before the action begins...

Eighteen-year-old defender Honest Ahanor starts in Palace’s back three alongside Jaydee Canvot, 20, and Chris Richards, 26. This afternoon will be a decent examination of their credentials as a unit. The Italy defender is on loan from Atalanta and will join Chelsea next summer.

The police-to-fan ratio looks fairly healthy here...

Palace fans head to #Brighton Station more on @brightonargus https://t.co/LQ9MKobmFH

Brighton’s form is all the more impressive given that Hurzeler has not had recourse to key men in Yankuba Minteh, Kaoru Mitoma and Mats Wieffer.

Femi Azeez, signed from Millwall in the summer for £15m, has only featured in a friendly match during the international break and remains sidelined with a muscle issue.

These missing men are nearing returns, and it makes you wonder whether Brighton can reach even further heights.

There will be supporters of both sides who are not particularly moved by this match-up. Some Crystal Palace fans may argue that their rivalry with Nottingham Forest has been more intense in recent years.

When asked about the rivalry, Sage said: “I know that the fans don’t like this name [the M23 derby] because it is too far to name it this. We know it is a big game for the club and the fans, and we have to show our better phases, like the second halves of our last two games.”

Interestingly, the categories in which Brighton have excelled marry up almost perfectly with Crystal Palace’s weakest areas. Here are their numbers in the same/reciprocal departments:

Brighton’s fast start to the season has been evidenced by league-leading numbers in key departments, particularly in the attacking third.

What is it? Well, I have been reliably advised that this is a take on a social media trend where implausible, dystopian AI videos are set to the song Storm II by GENER8ION featuring Yung Lean (don’t worry, me neither).

While some may argue that Palace’s roller-coaster 2025-26 season was at times dystopian (just ask Marc Guéhi or Oliver Glasner), the Europa League trophy is very much real. No AI needed here.

Pascal previews today's test... 💬 https://t.co/Cgj4APvfi4

"We have to play with passion and energy" Régis Le Bris speaks ahead of Sunderland's visit to Bournemouth 🎙️ https://t.co/KgWfOi4Pt5

Palace have conceded in the first 20 minutes of three of their six league games this season, and within the first 10 minutes in their last two outings.

It is a concern Sage acknowledged in his pre-match press conference: “It’s difficult to explain… We just have to put altogether the conditions to start well to make a good game in the whole of this one [against Brighton]. I think we are able to do it, we did it in Leeds, now we are in this situation.

“We are aware of what’s happened in these two games [against Forest and Lyon], one was a good result, one was a bad result, but in each game, when we are 100 per cent on what we have to do in our gameplan, I think we are able to do really wonderful things. When we are not like this, it is another story.”

Brighton have played against 10 men twice this season but were consigned to that very fate last weekend at the Stadium of Light.

Having gone ahead through De Cuyper, Struijk was given his marching orders (a decision that has since been overturned on appeal) and the visitors were made to show a different side to their character, battling in a deep block and frustrating Sunderland before adding a second.

"Today it's up to us" Marco Rose is hoping for Bournemouth's first league win of the season 🍒 https://t.co/VoNR9VfCOd

Pascal Gross may be 35 years old, but he is enjoying one of the finest seasons of his career, creating the most chances in the Premier League. Of his midfield talisman, Hurzeler said: “It started in pre-season. During pre-season he’s never the person who can lay on the beach for several hours doing nothing…

“He really suffered in pre-season. In pre-season you really build a foundation for the whole season, you build a physical foundation, a resilience, you build also the mindset… How he came back after this break was impressive. He looked so fit, so sharp, so ready… We saw a different face from him already and then it’s just a progression for him on the pitch…

“Of course no one expected it would be that good, but shows that he still has all this capacity in his body.”

Neither Brobbey nor Isidor make the match-day squad, so it will be up to 21-year-old Tutyerov to lead the line for Sunderland.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German said: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

You can also follow the latest updates from Manchester United’s crucial trip to Elland Road in our sister blog here.

#1270. Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of \({\mathcal{O}}(1)\) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

#1269. New Waterfront Masterplan Builds On Hill Dickinson Stadium Transformation

Liverpool City Council has approved an updated Liverpool Waters masterplan, marking another significant milestone in the regeneration of the city’s northern waterfront and building on the transformation brought about by the development of Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The revised planning framework, brought forward by Peel Waters, will guide the next phase of development across the 60-hectare site stretching from Everton's headquarters at The Royal Liver Building to the Club’s new waterfront home at Bramley-Moore Dock.

The development of Hill Dickinson Stadium has acted as a catalyst for the regeneration of North Liverpool, stimulating investment, creating employment opportunities, attracting visitors and unlocking the potential of a previously underutilised area of the city.

The updated masterplan reflects the significant changes that have taken place along Liverpool’s waterfront since the original planning consent was granted in 2013, most notably the development of Everton’s new home and its emergence as a major sporting, entertainment and visitor destination.

The refreshed plans will support the delivery of new homes, including affordable housing, alongside high-quality public spaces, healthcare provision, community facilities, employment opportunities and sustainable infrastructure across five distinctive waterfront neighbourhoods.

Central to the plans is the creation of a new five-acre waterfront park at Central Docks. Already under construction as part of Liverpool Waters’ £81 million infrastructure investment programme, the park will feature more than 3,000 trees and is expected to open in spring 2028.

The park and wider development will provide new and enhanced pedestrian routes through the northern docks, offering supporters and visitors an optional attractive walking route between Liverpool city centre and Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Alongside new leisure and hospitality destinations, the creation of these public spaces will help transform the matchday and non-matchday journey for Evertonians, providing more opportunities for supporters to spend time along the waterfront before and after fixtures and major events at the stadium.

The increased focus on pedestrian connectivity, active travel and sustainable transport also complements Everton’s ongoing work with key stakeholders to improve accessibility to Hill Dickinson Stadium and better connect the Club’s waterfront home with the city centre and surrounding communities.

Colin Chong, Everton’s Chief Real Estate and Regeneration Officer, said: “From the outset, our ambition for Hill Dickinson Stadium extended far beyond delivering a new home for Everton Football Club. It was also about unlocking the potential of Liverpool’s northern waterfront and providing a catalyst for wider investment, regeneration and economic growth.

“We are already seeing the positive impact of the stadium on the surrounding area, with new businesses establishing themselves and existing businesses benefiting from increased footfall and activity.

“The updated Liverpool Waters masterplan provides an opportunity to build on that momentum. New public spaces, improved walking routes and better connectivity will complement our own investment in establishing Hill Dickinson Stadium and our Budweiser Plaza as a year-round destination, enhancing the appeal of the area, attracting more visitors and creating further opportunities for businesses, investment and employment across North Liverpool.”

The growing programme of major sporting and entertainment events at Hill Dickinson Stadium is extending the economic benefits of Everton’s investment beyond football matchdays and across the wider Liverpool City Region.

As well as being the home for Everton's Premier League fixtures, Hill Dickinson Stadium has already hosted an international football fixture between Scotland and Côte d’Ivoire, a Rugby League Ashes Test, Magic WKND and a Rugby Union Nations Championship fixture, the stadium will also host matches during UEFA EURO 2028, with a programme of major concerts at the Club’s waterfront home set to get under way in summer 2027.

The ability to attract events of national and international significance is helping to further strengthen Liverpool’s reputation as a global sporting, cultural and entertainment destination, drawing additional visitors to the city, supporting its hotel, hospitality, retail and transport sectors, and creating further opportunities for investment and employment across the region.

Since the original Liverpool Waters masterplan was approved in 2013, the northern waterfront has undergone significant change, with the delivery of new residential developments, transport infrastructure, leisure and hospitality destinations and public spaces, alongside Hill Dickinson Stadium and the Isle of Man Ferry Terminal.

James Whittaker, Managing Director of Peel Waters, said: “The approval of the updated Liverpool Waters masterplan marks another major milestone in the transformation of Liverpool’s northern waterfront. Since the original masterplan was approved in 2013, we have delivered significant progress across the site, including new homes, public spaces, leisure destinations, major transport infrastructure and the new Everton Stadium, helping establish Liverpool Waters as one of the UK’s most ambitious regeneration projects.

“This updated framework reflects the considerable investment already made by Peel Waters and our partners, while providing the flexibility needed to respond to evolving market demand and future opportunities. With over £81 million of infrastructure investment committed at Central Docks, Princes Dock nearing completion and a clear vision for future neighbourhoods, Liverpool Waters is entering an exciting new chapter that will continue to create homes, jobs, investment and opportunities for Liverpool and the wider city region.”

The revised framework also strengthens commitments around sustainability, biodiversity, climate resilience and the preservation of Liverpool’s rich maritime heritage – principles that were central to the development of Everton’s waterfront home.

Pete Swift, CEO and Co-Founder, Planit – the landscape architecture, urban design and masterplanning studio who also worked as part of the team to deliver Everton's new home, added: “We are overjoyed at the approval, not just for the Peel Waters and Liverpool Waters team but for the communities of Liverpool.

“A network of green and blue spaces, with the central park at the heart, now forms the backbone for our neighbourhoods. We understand better the assets that sit below the ground and the history on and above it – views old and new structure the place.

“Hill Dickinson stadium changes the game; literally – for Everton Football Club and North Liverpool. It was never in the original masterplan [from 2013] and so we must adapt to respond to it and the opportunities it brings. Our wider variety of homes now represents a more inclusive, family-focused, inter-generational Liverpool Waters.

“Today’s consent embodies Peel Waters’ future-facing attitude and commitment to the quality of buildings and their supporting infrastructure – to remake a place that will play a major role in North Liverpool’s sustainable future.”

The approved masterplan retains Liverpool Waters’ five-neighbourhood structure comprising Princes Dock, KINGS, Central Docks, Clarence Docks and Northern Docks.

Liverpool Waters also sits within the proposed Liverpool City Region Mayoral Development Zone, an initiative designed to accelerate regeneration, support investment and unlock the delivery of new homes, jobs and infrastructure.

The approval of Peel Waters' updated masterplan represents the next stage in the evolution of Liverpool’s northern waterfront, building on the investment made by Everton in delivering Hill Dickinson Stadium and the Club’s longstanding ambition for its new home to be a driver of economic growth, regeneration and lasting opportunities for North Liverpool and the wider city region.

#1268. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area showed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

“It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

“We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

“They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”

Brighton & Hove Albion 5 Crystal Palace 0

It’s all over at Elland Road, with Leeds and Man Utd playing out a competitive draw. Mbeumo’s opener was cancelled out by Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser in a game that was low on attacking quality and chances. Ultimately, a draw was a very fair reflection of the match. Man Utd are 14th and winless in six games across all competitions, while Leeds move into the top seven.

FULL-TIME: Dominic Calvert-Lewin earns a point for Leeds against Manchester United 💪 https://t.co/yDzLRE3Ir5

There are two yellow cards in quick succession as Ampadu is cautioned for a late tackle on Amad. Andrey Santos runs over and barges into the Leeds captain to earn himself a booking. The referee quickly calms then drama down.

Unconvincing goalkeeping from Lammens as he only punches Ampadu’s cross as far as Stach, whose tame shot squeezes through the Belgian’s legs. However, it’s blocked by the Man Utd defence and Lammens eventually gathers the ball.

There will be four minutes of added time. Can either side snatch a late victory?

Three times now United have looked like they’re about to get away down the flanks in the last few minutes and each time they’ve been flagged offside (Amad twice, Mbeumo once) and each occasion the player was able to look across the line. Carrick looked to the heavens. And he’s right to be frustrated. So avoidable.

Nmecha and Maguire challenge for the ball in the air, with the Man Utd defender bumping into the back of the Leeds substitute’s head. The crowd half-heartedly appeal for a penalty, but it’s quickly checked and cleared by VAR.

Carrick responds with a positive, attacking switch as Tielemans departs for Cunha.

Farke makes another change for Leeds as Longstaff replaces Tanaka in midfield.

Excellently goalkeeping from Trafford, who dashes out of his six-yard box to collect Andrey Santos’ pass and keep the ball in his grasp while staying in his box under the watchful eye of Mbeumo.

Dalot drives forward and leads a counter-attack. He passes to Amad, who forces a corner as Leeds get back well and recover. Man Utd take a clever short corner routine, but it ends with Mount scuffing an effort wide.

Both teams make changes. For Leeds, Nmecha replaces Okafor, while Mount enters the action for Man Utd as Baleba is withdrawn. The Englishman will sit alongside Andrey Santos in the away side’s midfield pivot.

From presentable range, Fernandes curls an effort straight into Trafford’s arms. Dalot then fails to adequately deal with a cross, heading the ball only as far as Stach. However, the Leeds midfielder wildly lashes his strike over the bar.

United were under that cosh in that period after Leeds equalised but they’ve gained a foothold back in the game now and a bit of frustration has crept in among the home fans. Stach the third player to fire high over the bar. Could go either way this.

How much longer will Carrick wait before making some changes in forward areas? His side need some renewed attacking impetus. The Man Utd head coach has Rashford, Cunha, Mount and Zirkzee all on the bench to choose from.

Okafor attempts to spearhead a Leeds break by playing in Calvert-Lewin. However, his pass is poor and it’s intercepted by Maguire. Amad is down after being caught by Tanaka earlier in that phase of play.

On the turn, Fernandes drags a low effort wide of the far post in a rare attacking flurry for Man Utd in this second half.

Ampadu feels Leeds should have a penalty as he collides with Maguire at a corner. The Man Utd defender hauls the Leeds captain to the floor. It’s been checked and cleared by VAR, but Maguire was taking a huge risk there.

Michael Carrick will surely be angry at the way Manchester United have started the second-half. One-nil up they have been far too slow and casual - highlighted by Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s goal which was embarrassingly easy to score from a corner. Leeds now on top and a huge few minutes ahead for Carrick.

Gudmundsson’s searching cross can’t quite find Calvert-Lewin as Man Utd scramble it clear. The away side’s backline has three defenders playing out of position, and they’ve been made to pay by Leeds’ leveller.

How will Man Utd cope with that setback? Leeds are putting them under serious pressure and have flown out of the blocks since the break as Tanaka volleys over from outside the penalty area.

The hosts finally have something to shout about at Elland Road! Leeds have a corner and Muharemovic beats Mazraoui to the delivery. The defender glances the ball to Calvert-Lewin, who holds off Mbeumo before smashing a close-range half-volley into the bottom corner. Elland Road goes wild and Leeds now have the momentum at the start of this second half.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm

It looks like a straight swap as Mazraoui slots in as a centre back, with Yoro continuing to deputise on the right.

We are back under way the second half. Martinez has been withdrawn at half-time, with Mazraoui on as his replacement, while Leeds are unchanged.

That is a really good half for Manchester United. More for the scoreline than the performance, although they have grown into the game after a sluggish start. Bryan Mbeumo’s goal will come as a huge relief to Michael Carrick. Leeds, in truth, have been a disappointment although they were denied the opening goal by Senne Lammens with a fine save. They needs to raise the tempo and the crowd. It is far too quiet. If Manchester United can hold on or build on this it will be a huge result for their under-pressure manager.

Carrick will be delighted with that first half. Man Utd have frustrated Leeds, defended valiantly and found the all-important breakthrough thanks to Mbeumo’s opener. Despite all the drama leading up to this game, Man Utd look really organised and unified, limiting Leeds to very little in forward areas.

Ahead at the break 👊🔴 https://t.co/rSSC8Pu4iG

There will be two minutes of added time. Can Man Utd protect their lead until the break?

Bogle drives into Man Utd’s box and squeezes a shot through a sea of bodies. However, it trickles into Lammens’ arms.

A big few minutes here for Manchester United. They need to see this half out. The goal has really steadied them but important they take that lead into the interval.

Calvert-Lewin attempts to latch onto Bogle’s clipped cross, but he directs it harmlessly wide.

Carrick’s game plan has worked perfectly so far. Man Utd soaked up the early pressure with their determined defending, before growing in confidence over the last 10 minutes. Mbeumo’s goal was much deserved.

You could see what that goal meant to Michael Carrick. He’s not one to show his emotions but he punches the air and wears the steely look of a man who knows how important it was to get the first goal here.

Mbeumo missed an earlier chance, but he makes no mistake with that one! Amad slips in Tielemans, who whips a magnificent cross into Mbeumo. The forward shows great composure and guides the delivery into the bottom corner.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

The crowd loves that as Trafford sprints way out of his box almost to the halfway line to beat Amad to a ball over the top. Man Utd then make a promising break through Mbeumo, whose tame effort is easily gathered by Trafford.

Bogle attempts to take everyone on as he dribbles into Man Utd’s penalty area. He glides away from Dalot and Martinez, but overruns it, allowing Maguire to come across and shepherd the ball out of play.

Chants of “you soft southern b------” from the Leeds fans every time a Manchester United player goes down injured. Just a reminder that Leeds is actually only 22 miles further north than Manchester.

The away side are growing into this contest, with a slick move seeing Baleba find Dalot. The right back sprints into Leeds’ box, but he’s tackled well by Bogle.

Mbeumo misses a massive opportunity! Tielemans clips in a cross and an unmarked Mbeumo finds space between Elvedi and Muharemovic but heads wide. He has to get that on target.

Bryan Mbeumo comes close to giving Manchester United the lead 😬 https://t.co/j5PFXa2Uhe

Leeds test Lammens! Stach whips in a free kick, which is met by Elvedi, whose downward header is parried away by Lammens. That’s Leeds’ best chance so far, but the Man Utd goalkeeper did his job.

Leeds have enjoyed nearly 70% possession, but they’re yet to have a shot of any note. That’s testament to Man Utd’s competitiveness and organisation. Bogle then digs out a promising cross, but Yoro heads it away at the back post.

In fairness to Man Utd, they’re defending solidly and doing well to frustrate Leeds. Gudmundsson is then carded for catching Andrey Santos on his ankle with a very unpleasant challenge. It’s been such a physical and scruffy match so far.

Risky from Fernandes as he lunges in with a dangerous challenge on Muharemovic. Leeds then break as Martinez misses his tackle on Calvert-Lewin, but Stach’s cross is blocked. When the ball eventually goes out of play, Fernandes is booked for that earlier challenge. He can have no complaints.

United staff aggrieved that Fernandes should be booked but Ampadu escape a yellow card before then for arguably a worse challenge on Mbeumo, whom he caught thick on the ankle with his studs.

🫡 Ethan Ampadu starts as captain for the 100th time, becoming the youngest player to reach that milestone since Billy Bremner! https://t.co/80YrU08S3s

No early rhythm in this game so far. It’s still a little frantic at the moment, with Leeds having most of the ball and trying to force the issue.

Leeds crunch into a couple of heavy challenges on the Man Utd players in these early exchanges. Stach is eventually penalised for a strong tackle, but it’s a purposeful start from the hosts.

Interestingly, it looks like Fernandes is starting centrally in the ‘false nine’ position, with Mbeumo and Amad out on the wings. The Man Utd captain started out wide in Spain on Wednesday - an experiment that definitely did not work.

We are under way at Elland. Can Leeds pile more misery on Man Utd or will the visitors answer their critics with a much-needed win?

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was the only player not to take the knee prior to kick-off for the Premier League’s ‘No Room for Racism’ campaign. The gesture from the other players was roundly booed by a lot of the fans inside Elland Road.

Both teams are out on the pitch, with kick-off fast approaching.

With just 10 minutes until kick-off, here’s a recap of the two squads.

Leeds: Trafford, Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic, Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin.

Subs: Zetterer, Longstaff, Wilson, Aaronson, Nmecha, Bijol, Bahoya, Bard, Gruev.

Man Utd: Lammens, Yoro, Maguire, Martinez, Dalot, Santos, Baleba, Fernandes, Tielemans, Diallo, Mbeumo.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, de Ligt, Mount, Rashford, Cunha, Zirkzee, Lacey, Amass.

Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and said he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

With all eyes on the visitors, Leeds will be licking their lips at the prospect of piling further misery on their beleaguered opponents. Daniel Farke’s side suffered their first Premier League loss last weekend, falling 2-1 to Arsenal at the Emirates after going a goal up, but the mood remains positive after a solid start to the campaign.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

Unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

This has all the ingredients to be a thrilling and fascinating watch as we bring you the latest updates, information and drama. Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

#1267. How EitC Helped Sean Realise He's Not Alone After His Wife's Tragic Passing

This Christmas, a lifelong Evertonian is sharing how Everton in the Community helped him survive the loneliest time of his life after his wife died just 12 hours after the birth of their second son.

Sean Foster, from Wigan, lost his wife Taylor in the early hours of 1 July 2020. Taylor was just 25 years old and passed away due to a splenic artery aneurysm, after being found unresponsive by staff on the mother and baby ward. 

Sean faced the devastating reality of raising two young children without his wife, while navigating grief, anxiety and suicidal thoughts.

He said: “I’ve been through grief before, but this was something else.

“You’re not just grieving for the person you’ve lost; it’s the future you had with them, it’s what they’ll miss out on with the kids and what the kids will miss out on with having their mum.

“With grief also came overwhelming struggles with PTSD, depression, anxiety and suicidal ideation. One thing that accompanies grief, which I have found the hardest and most persistent to cope with, is loneliness.”

Just six days after Taylor's death, Sean reached out to Everton in the Community on Twitter (now X) in the middle of the night – a decision he described as his “hail Mary” and the first step towards seeking help. 

“My newborn baby and his two-year-old brother were asleep, and I found myself feeling completely alone, drowning in grief and crying uncontrollably.

“It was a hail Mary. I just needed to reach out to someone and, as an Evertonian, I knew about Everton in the Community – but I didn’t expect the level of help I did get. It was a lifesaver.” 

A donation to Everton in the Community this Christmas will help the official charity of Everton Football Club to support more people like Sean and to ensure no one has to face loneliness alone.

Although Sean had immense support from friends and family, he didn’t want to worry them.

He continued: “By lunchtime, I had a response from Everton in the Community and just a couple of hours after that I was on the phone with them.

“The support I got from them was second to none and I know I would have found that period of my life so much harder if I hadn’t reached out.”

Donate to Everton in the Community

A member of Everton in the Community’s team visited Sean, providing essential items to help him care for his two young sons. 

 The charity's wellbeing team also signposted him to additional organisations for grief support, while regular phone calls gave Sean someone to turn to during some of his most difficult moments.  

He also received support in navigating practical challenges, including his finances and helping his children understand what had happened. Sean received a call from Everton legend Duncan Ferguson on the day Taylor's cause of death was confirmed.  

Taking the time to ask Sean about his wife and what she was like, the conversation marked an important moment in his journey, helping him take the first steps towards talking about Taylor again. 

 “Taylor was a force to be reckoned with,” Sean said. “She was genuinely one of a kind. A lot of people will say it about her, she was so thoughtful and she always looked out for others before herself.

“Even the gifts she’d give on birthdays and Christmas, she’d know exactly what each person wanted and needed, make a care package, wrap it nicely and put a bow on it.

“She was really into her arts and crafts and my eldest, he had two years with her, one of the things he always remembers is colouring with his mum.” 

Reflecting on the importance of having someone to turn to, Sean says he dreads to think about what might have happened had he not reached out to EitC. 

“I was in a really dark place and considering suicide," he admitted. "It’s not that I wanted to die. I wanted the kids to have a full family, a mum and dad figure and a safe, stable home. At that point in time I didn’t think I was giving them that. If I hadn’t reached out or got a response, I really struggle to think where I’d be.”

Sean has since become an advocate for men’s mental health, including volunteering for Andy’s Man Club and starting his own podcast about grief. He has received therapy and attends group support sessions where he passionately talks about issues such as loneliness. 

He said: “The loneliest I have ever felt was at Christmas, the year Taylor died. All my family were crammed into my mum and dad's house, as we do every year, all 20-plus of us in the living room, scrambling to find our pile of presents as we did every year.  

“Only this year, Taylor wasn’t there laughing at the Christmas chaos. To this day I have never felt as lonely as I did in that moment.”

Although he still experiences moments of loneliness, Sean says the support he has received has helped him understand that he doesn't have to face them alone.

He hopes that by sharing his experience, he can encourage others who may be struggling to reach out, particularly during a time of year when feelings of loneliness can become more difficult.

Sean said: “Loneliness isn’t the same as being alone.

“We can have people around us, we can see friends, family, colleagues daily, but we can still feel lonely. 

“What I found about loneliness, particularly as a man, is that there's a stigma around talking about it, there's an expectation that we should just be strong, just get on with it and deal with it ourselves.   

“Most of the time that is the expectation we put on ourselves, when the fact is the real strength is in asking for help, admitting we might need a hand every now and then. 

“I still experience moments of loneliness, but they aren't as all-consuming. Thanks to Everton in the Community, I've learned I'm never truly alone.” 

A donation to Everton in the Community this Christmas could help someone facing loneliness find the support they need – someone to listen and somewhere to turn when things feel impossible.

#1266. FIFA hit by cyberattack with 'personal and business information' stolen - including immigration documents and financial records - after hackers 'impersonated staff'

Published: 07:12 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 08:10 EST, 26 November 2026

Personal information, immigration documents and financial records have been stolen from FIFA in a cyberattack.

Football's governing body confirmed that a hacking group 'impersonated staff' to gain access to their system before taking the sensitive files.

In total, more than 12 gigabytes of data has been stolen and a group called Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) shared a screenshot of FIFA documents on X last week, claiming credit for the theft and finding access through FIFA’s Microsoft app portal.

They are understood to have then published the stolen files on a forum on the dark web, writing 'more leaks soon'.

A FIFA spokesperson said: 'FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyber-attack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information.

'FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.

FIFA were hacked and had sensitive documents stolen - pictured, FIFA president Gianni Infantino

Handsome Boy Hacking Club took credit for the hack and shared this screenshot on X

'FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data.

According to the Athletic, immigration, financial and personal documents were stolen by the hackers impersonating staff but did not include the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a plan to effectively sell off the World Cup that collapsed and piled pressure on president Gianni Infantino.

The FFE plan first became public knowledge in July. Infantino sought to create a company to manage the commercial interests of FIFA’s competitions, including the World Cup, but wanted a minority stake to be made available to private investors.

The lead investor was set to be Thrive, a company founded by President Trump’s son-in-law’s brother, Josh Kushner, but the plan was abandoned on August 1 after three continental confederations rejected it.

It remains to be seen whether files relating to Infantino himself were taken by the hackers.

The 56-year-old is currently running for reelection against Kohzo Tashima of Japan and France football federation president Philippe Diallo.

He remains the strong favorite to win FIFA's election is held on March 18 and has already served three terms.

FIFA are the latest football-related body to have fallen victim to cyber crime, with LaLiga targeted earlier this month.

Spanish police are still investigating but LaLiga confirmed their security teams identified the source and stopped the hacker from stealing more data.

#1265. Everton Announces Partnership With Global Risk & Insurance Specialist WTW

Everton has confirmed a new multi-year partnership with WTW, a leading global advisory, broking and solutions company, as the Club continues to expand its commercial portfolio into new categories.

The agreement sees WTW become Everton’s ‘Official Insurance Partner’, bringing specialist expertise in insurance, risk management and analytics to support the Club’s operations and long-term ambitions.

Operating across more than 140 countries and markets, WTW becomes the latest internationally-recognised business to join Everton’s growing partnership portfolio, following recent agreements with NOCO, Nestlé and JYSK. 

Through the agreement, WTW will benefit from brand visibility at Hill Dickinson Stadium and across Everton’s digital and social media channels as well as commercial activation opportunities through access to the Club’s waterfront home for client hospitality, business events and engagement activities. The agreement allows for wider collaboration, including community initiatives, that will also be explored.

As Everton’s exclusive partner in the insurance brokerage category, WTW will also provide tailored risk and insurance advice and solutions, drawing on its global insurance-market relationships and extensive experience across the sports and entertainment industry.

Mark Rollings, Chief Partnerships Officer at Everton, said: “We are delighted to welcome WTW as our Official Insurance Partner.

“WTW is a highly respected global business with an outstanding reputation for expertise and innovation. This is a relationship that brings together two organisations with shared ambitions and a commitment to long-term success.

“Alongside the international profile and opportunities Everton can offer WTW, the partnership will bring valuable specialist knowledge to the Club and create opportunities for collaboration beyond traditional sponsorship.

“Welcoming another business of WTW’s calibre is a further demonstration of our commercial momentum and the growing appeal of Everton to leading international organisations.”

WTW has an established presence across the global sports and entertainment sector, working with some the world’s best-known professional clubs, governing bodies, sporting events and venues to manage complex risks, strengthen resilience and support performance.

Ian Tomlin, Global Sports and Entertainment Leader at WTW, said: “High-performing organisations, whether in sport or business, depend on resilience, specialist expertise and the confidence to make informed decisions.

“Our partnership with Everton brings together the Club’s ambition and distinctive identity with WTW’s global insurance, risk and analytics expertise.

“Together, we will help create greater resilience, improved risk management and performance, and lasting value on and off the pitch.”

Read a snippet from the interview below and buy your matchday programme online or at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday!

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall played an integral role in the historic first derby match hosted at Hill Dickinson Stadium, producing a slide-rule cross for Beto to become the first Everton goalscorer at our new home in a derby match.

The occasion lived up to expectations.

“It was electric,” Dewsbury-Hall tells the Official Matchday Programme. “It was amazing to be part of the first one at the new stadium.

“The atmosphere was electric, it was mental. It was feisty in the first half, with a lot of crunching tackles and a lot of physicality. The last minute apart, it was a good occasion to be a part of.

“It’s always a feisty game! It’s always a game which is exciting, so it was a nice feeling to know I’d be involved in them when I signed for Everton.

“The two I played in last year were pretty exciting. Obviously, they didn’t end the best for us, especially with the last-minute goal here. But for me it was a taste of what the fixture was like. So I’m very excited to experience it again.”

The fixture in April was the 214th league clash between the two old rivals, but the first not to have been staged at either Anfield or Goodison Park.

All Premier League matches are famously competitive, but Dewsbury-Hall admits there is definitely something special when Everton and Liverpool collide.

“It is a little bit different,” he admits. “Of course it’s a high-profile fixture, but there’s the added incentive of it being a derby. Naturally it gets spoken about before the game, how important it is.

“I mean, there’s a lot of staff here who support the Club. They let you know exactly what it means to Everton.

"I knew that anyway, but they’re all like, ‘Come on! It’s a Merseyside derby! As long as we beat Liverpool!’ So, there’s always that added incentive.

“As players we know the importance of the fixture – if you can win this game it’s significant, because notoriously, over the past couple of years, Liverpool have been higher than us in the table. But we’re trying to close that gap now.”

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.
