#1237. Darren Bent's beach ball bedlam, Nani's controversial quick-thinking and Peter Enckelman's calamitous mishap: Our experts pick the strangest goals they have ever seen after Bruno Fernandes' 'divot strike' in Lisbon

Published: 15:03 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 15:03 EST, 26 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United were the beneficiaries of a bizarre goal in the Champions League on Wednesday night, as the captain's long-range effort bounced up off the turf and deceived the goalkeeper to help earn Mauricio Pochettino a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in his second game in charge.

Football has certainly seen its fair share of quirky, bizarre and downright bonkers goals over the years, and Fernandes' effort in Lisbon is certainly one to add to the collection.

Here, Daily Mail Sport's reporters look back at some of the strangest goals they can remember, from outrageous goalkeeping blunders to freakish deflections and moments of sheer misfortune.

Darren Bent (Sunderland 1-0 Liverpool) - October 17, 2009

Forget bouncing in off a divot, try the ball flying into the net off a beach ball. Darren Bent’s winner against Liverpool at the Stadium of Light back in 2009 has got to be the strangest.

A Liverpool fan lobbed a gigantic red beach ball on to the pitch (in the middle of October) which was initially removed by a steward only for the wind to blow it back.

What made it even funnier was that when Bent’s shot struck it, Liverpool keeper Pepe Reina tried to save the inflatable, which now resides in the National Football Museum, instead of the actual ball that flew past him.

Thank heavens there was no VAR back then to spoil the day.

Pepe Reina had no chance after Darren Bent's strike ricocheted off a beach ball into the goal

Peter Enckelman (Birmingham vs Aston Villa) - September 16, 2002

Obviously the mind immediately goes to balloons and players ghosting behind goalkeepers. But my favourite happened on September 16, 2002 between Birmingham City and Aston Villa.

Olof Mellberg took a throw-in. He threw it back to Peter Enckelman. The ball bounced under Enckelman’s foot and rolled into the Villa goal. Referee David Elleray reckoned he must have touched it with his studs.

It was all made worse for Enckelman with a Birmingham fan hopping out of the crowd to goad him to his face. I must have been nine years old and remember watching all this live.

Can’t imagine my parents told me what that hand gesture the fan was doing in front of Enckelman meant.

Peter Enckelman scored a disastrous own goal after the ball bounced underneath his foot

Mo Diame (Brighton vs Newcastle) - February 28, 2017

Brighton half cleared a corner and Christian Atsu returned a scuffed volley, which was helped on by the toe of Daryl Murphy, before Mo Diame planted his foot in the ground and allowed the ball to bounce off the back of his heel, looping up and over all inside the goalmouth and into the top corner.

I was there, and I have revisited my match report.

'Diame had been stood still for the majority of the previous 81 minutes,' I wrote. 'Finally, it was a tactic which served him well.'

I also refer to the goal as fluky and hilarious. It is now the stuff of legend on Tyneside, for it helped Newcastle to win promotion as champions. Indeed, without it, Brighton would have finished top and Newcastle second.

Mo Diame scored one of the craziest goals in Championship history against Brighton in 2017

Tony Popovic (Portsmouth vs Crystal Palace) - September 11, 2004

Some goals stay with you because of the sublime, others because of the ridiculous. And I doubt I'll ever see a stranger goal live than Tony Popovic's flying backheel into his own net in 2004.

With Portsmouth protecting a 2-1 lead late on against Crystal Palace, nerves were jangling around Fratton Park until Popovic's moment of spectacular misfortune.

Pompey's Steve Stone floated a hopeful cross into the Palace box, prompting Popovic to stretch out a leg in an attempt to clear. Instead, he somehow managed to flick the ball off his boot, onto the post and into the net, producing a finish any top striker would be proud of.

Portsmouth couldn't believe their luck when Tony Popovic flicked the ball into in his own net

Nani (Manchester United vs Tottenham) - October 30, 2010

This one has always stuck with me, partly for the sheer audacity of Nani and partly because it's the sort of goal that simply wouldn't escape VAR scrutiny today.

Back when a trip to Manchester United was still a fearsome prospect, Spurs were a goal down and chasing a late equaliser when Nani was brought down in the penalty area and appeared to handle the ball.

Crucially, though, Mark Clattenburg had not blown his whistle. Tottenham goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes, assuming a free-kick had been awarded, placed the ball on the ground.

Still gesticulating, Nani got up, realised the ball was still live, and coolly passed it into the back of the net. Cue bedlam in the Stretford End.

Nani celebrates his controversial goal against Spurs, to the fury of goalkeeper Heurelho Gomes

Zlatan Ibrahimovic (Sweden vs England) - November 14, 2012

It's not weird in the category of a divot or a beach ball but the most outlandish goal I've ever seen live was Zlatan Ibrahimovic's 30-yard overhead kick for Sweden against England at the Friends Arena in Stockholm in November 2012.

A long ball came over the top of the England defence, Joe Hart ran out and headed it clear and Ibrahimovic launched himself into the air, hooking the ball in a majestic arc over England's disbelieving goalkeeper. Great goals can be strange, too.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic's acrobatic bicycle kick against England was both strange and sensational

Stan Collymore (Blackburn vs Liverpool) - February 24, 1996

As soon as I watched Fernandes' speculative long-range strike bobble past Sporting Lisbon goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, my mind immediately cast back to Tim Flowers being embarrassed by Stan Collymore at Ewood Park in 1996.

Not that it was the Blackburn goalkeeper's fault, of course. Collymore's feeble effort from distance in the 11th minute trickled along the turf before hitting a rogue divot and bouncing over Flowers' head into the net.

Collymore, who cracked a smile but toned down his celebrations, turned away in disbelief as Flowers stared down at the pitch with his hands on his hips.

Liverpool went on to win the game 3-2 and Flowers described it as 'one of those ridiculous situations'.

Stan Collymore scored one of the strangest goals when his effort bobbled over Tim Flowers

Gary Neville (England vs Croatia) - October 11, 2006

Strange bobbles take me back to Gary Neville’s own goal in Zagreb. Early in the doomed England reign of Steve McClaren.

Neville rolled a simple back pass towards Paul Robinson who took a mighty swing at fresh air with his right boot and looked aghast as it trundled past him and into the net for Croatia's second in a 2-0 win. The Spurs keeper stamped furiously at the offending divot as the Maksimir Stadium erupted.

Adding another layer to the comic value were pitchside LED ad screens flashing up images of Sacha Baron Cohen’s new Borat film and one of his lame catchphrases: 'I like you'.

It was a bad omen at the start of the failed Euro 2008 campaign and the beginning of the end for both Robinson and Neville in England colours.

Gary Neville's own goal against Croatia came after Paul Robinson totally missed the ball

Stefan Kiessling (Hoffenheim v Leverkusen) - October 18, 2013

Legendary Bayer Leverkusen forward Stefan Kiessling has got to be one of the only players to score with a shot off target.

While away to Hoffenheim, a corner was swung in towards Leverkusen striker Kiessling, who, at first glance, simply headed home smartly.

But on closer inspection we can see that the ball was destined for the side netting and an inconspicuous hole in the side of the net let the ball slip in.

Even Kiessling himself had his head in his hands thinking he’d missed before turning around to see his teammates were celebrating.

Leverkusen's Stefan Kiessling must be one of the only players to score with a shot off target

Bayern Munich are reportedly keeping tabs on Derry Scherhant as they look to strengthen their attacking options, with the German winger emerging as a potential alternative to Luis Diaz.

The Bundesliga giants are assessing several targets ahead of the summer transfer window, and the Freiburg forward has attracted attention with his performances and growing reputation in German football.

According to Christian Falk, Bayern have scouted Scherhant as they consider adding another attacking player to their squad. The German international is seen as a fit for the club’s recruitment strategy, although opportunities for regular football in Munich could be limited.

The 24-year-old has established himself as an exciting talent, and his versatility across the attacking positions could make him an attractive option for Bayern. His situation is reportedly worth monitoring, as he is also considering his next career move.

Bayern are expected to revisit several names on their shortlist in the coming months, and Scherhant could become a serious candidate ahead of the summer window.

Bayern are also understood to have previously explored a move for Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha, but securing his signature now appears increasingly difficult.

The teenager impressed in Liverpool’s clash with Manchester United, strengthening belief that the Merseyside club will seek to secure his long-term future with a new contract.

Falk suggested Bayern had been prepared to offer around €70 million (£58.5m) for Ngumoha during the summer, but Liverpool rejected their approach. The German side had hoped another opportunity could emerge, potentially with the youngster approaching the final year of his contract.

However, his recent performances have made that scenario less likely, leaving Bayern potentially needing to explore alternative targets.

Scherhant could therefore be a more realistic option for the Bundesliga champions as they look to reinforce their attack without pursuing an increasingly difficult deal for Ngumoha.

#1235. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

Michael Carrick is not one of the Premier League’s more loquacious managers but supporters will be interested in what he has to say at his pre-Bournemouth press conference this afternoon.

The Manchester United manager is under severe pressure after a run of no wins in seven games across all competitions, and senior players are talking out of school in post-game interviews.

Just when it appeared a line had been drawn under Lisandro Martinez taking on technical director Jason Wilcox, Bruno Fernandes reached for a petrol can and poured more fuel on the flames.

Speaking after the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes called out Carrick and his coaching staff for their tactical approach, specifically a reluctance to press opponents aggressively in a man-to-man fashion.

Carrick, by his own very measured standards, delivered a pointed response.

“We actually were half-pressed man to man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” he said. “And there’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Their opponents on Sunday are Bournemouth, who after a lean run of results under Marco Rose have just dispatched Sunderland for their first league victory of the season, and the mighty AC Milan in the Europa League.

Things do not get easier for United, who go to Stamford Bridge next weekend before a home game against Aston Villa before the November international break.

Telegraph Sport reported on Thursday that former Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann features prominently and is understood to want the job – as does Antonio Conte. United are also tracking Fabian Hurzeler while there is interest in Eddie Howe.

United are currently 13th in the table with seven points from seven games.

Tottenham Hotspur striker Richarlison is reportedly keen on returning to Everton, with the Brazilian international considering a reunion with his former club ahead of the January transfer window.

The 29-year-old has endured a frustrating spell in north London and appears increasingly likely to seek a fresh challenge after falling out of favour under manager Roberto De Zerbi.

#1233. Monaco defeat isn't fatal to our hopes of progressing in Europe, insists defiant Hearts manager Wouter Vrancken

Published: 16:37 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 16:38 EST, 26 November 2026

Wouter Vrancken claimed that Monaco’s 94th-minute winner at Tynecastle has not significantly diminished Hearts’ chances of reaching the knockout phase of the UEFA Conference League.

Vrancken’s team were left sickened when Folarin Balogun’s goal settled a thrilling contest in stoppage time to condemn them to a third consecutive defeat in the league phase of the competition after their away losses to Trabzonspor and Thun.

Hearts, who have just one point from their opening night draw at home to Nordsjaelland, now have to win both of their remaining games – at home to Bosnian side Borac on December 10 and away to Pafos in Cyprus a week later – to have any chance of further progress.

‘I don’t think losing that point makes a difference,’ insisted Vrancken. ‘The pleasing thing for me was that at 2-2 we still wanted to go and try to win the game.

‘Three points would have made a difference — zero or one point tonight doesn’t make a difference towards the next two games. We have to win them both now, so that doesn’t change.’

Vrancken took pride from Hearts’ display against their Ligue 1 opponents as two spectacular strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota cancelled out a Balogun penalty and Edan Diop’s goal in a breathless first half.

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken consoles goalscorer Sabah Kerjota as he is substituted

While Balogun’s late winner was harsh on Hearts, Vrancken believes his players paid the price for poor game management and was critical of the contribution of subs Josh McPake, Finlay Pollock and James Wilson who came on in the closing stages of the game.

‘It did feel cruel but at the same time we have to learn from that situation,’ said Vrancken. ‘Until then, we were really solid in not giving chances away.

‘I expect more from the guys who came on. We can win the ball with fresh players or make a foul somewhere to keep the result. I expect that kind of battling for the team, so we can do better there.

‘But the biggest thing is the performance we put on the park tonight against a really good side, knowing that we still have nine injuries and still do that against them. I’m really proud of them.

‘The goals we scored were really good and you see the confidence those guys have. They have taken confidence from the dynamics of what we did against Dundee at the weekend. The conviction in both boxes was there tonight and that’s important for us to take into the next run of games.’

Vrancken had no real complaint with Monaco’s penalty, awarded for a foul by Jamie McCart on Matthis Abline, but was unhappy that German referee Daniel Schlager failed to spot a foul on Kerjota before the visitors’ second goal.

Hearts players revel in the celebrations after Kerjota's wondergoal sent Tynecastle wild

‘For me, the penalty was light but okay,’ added the Belgian. ‘But if you are really decisive to give a penalty there, then you don’t see one of our players having his shirt pulled in the build-up to their second goal, that’s frustrating.

‘At this level, things can happen like this. It wasn’t given for us and it wasn’t the only decision like that tonight.’

Monaco coach Filipe Luis revelled in his team’s late win but admitted even he felt like joining in the acclamation of Kerjota’s goal for Hearts.

‘Hearts were a tough opponent and I knew it would be difficult,’ said Luis. ‘We found spaces and created chances from the start but Hearts scored a fantastic goal to go ahead.

‘But we stayed calm and scored twice before they scored another fantastic goal. It was so good, I almost had to applaud it!

‘Hearts didn’t create many chances in the second half and in the end we managed to win, so there are many good things for us tonight.’

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias was disappointed with an underwhelming performance.

He said: “Frustrating, I felt like we fought a lot. For the first 10-15 minutes of the first half we took our time to get into the game.

”It is what it is. Whatever happens we need to react to it. The team had a very good reaction. The second one was tough because it was very close to our equaliser. We kept going and tried to create chances. Not our day but we keep moving forward.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#1231. An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

West Ham United are reportedly facing a significant financial setback involving Pablo, with a potential January departure now looking increasingly likely after a disappointing spell at the London Stadium.

The Hammers are understood to have received an offer containing a purchase option worth just £2.5 million for the Brazilian striker, despite investing considerably more to secure his services earlier this year.

Reports suggest the East London outfit are concerned about the dramatic decline in the forward’s market value ahead of the January transfer window.

West Ham signed the 22-year-old from Gil Vicente in January 2026 for an initial £18.3 million, with a further £2.6 million included in potential add-ons.

However, Pablo has struggled to justify that investment, managing just two goals in 28 appearances across all competitions.

According to Claret & Hugh, several clubs have explored a temporary move, although one proposal reportedly includes an option to make the transfer permanent for only £2.5 million.

Such a valuation represents an enormous drop from West Ham’s original investment, leaving the club facing the prospect of a substantial financial loss.

The Brazilian’s situation has become increasingly complicated following Scott Parker’s appointment earlier this month.

The new manager has not included Pablo in any of his four matchday squads since taking charge, raising further doubts about his prospects of securing regular first-team football.

He has also struggled to make an impression in the Championship, scoring just once in nine league appearances this season.

West Ham could therefore consider arranging a loan move rather than accepting such a disappointing permanent transfer fee.

A successful spell elsewhere, potentially in Portugal, could help the striker rebuild his confidence and restore some of his market value.

For now, the Hammers must decide how best to limit their losses.

#1229. Hearts 2-3 Monaco: Late agony for brave hosts in Conference League tie - as Folarin Balogun strikes at the death to settle rollercoaster Tynecastle epic

Published: 15:54 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 17:41 EST, 26 November 2026

On a pulsating but ultimately painful evening for Hearts, their bid to reach the knockout phase of the UEFA Conference League suffered an agonising 94th-minute blow after they had gone toe-to-toe with a classy Monaco side.

USA World Cup striker Folarin Balogun’s stoppage-time winner preserved the Ligue 1 club’s perfect record in the league stage of the tournament and leaves Wouter Vrancken’s men with no remaining room for error.

Hearts must now win their last two games next month, at home to Bosnian side Borac and away to Pafos in Cyprus, to finish on seven points which could still be enough to secure a top 24 place in the 36-team standings.

It was a sickening conclusion to a thrilling match which saw Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota both score goal-of-the-season contenders for Hearts in a rollercoaster first half in which Balogun and Edan Diop were on target for Monaco.

Hearts emerged from the night with plenty of credit for their bold and often enterprising approach but it is points rather than plaudits they now need if their European campaign is to carry on beyond Christmas.

This would have been a challenging assignment for Hearts under any circumstances but the degree of difficulty was increased for Vrancken’s side by their injury list.

USA striker Folarin Balogun celebrates the late goal that broke hearts at Tynecastle

While easing slightly in recent weeks, with Blair Spittal the latest welcome returnee as he took a place on the bench, it remains significant and the Hearts coach was only able to name six outfield players among his subs.

With winger Josh McPake a surprising omission from the starting line-up, Vrancken sought greater solidity with the inclusion of 19-year-old defensive midfielder Matty Gillies.

After two sub outings since being recalled from his loan at Stenhousemuir, it was a baptism of fire for the teenager as he made his first start for Hearts.

Along with his more experienced team-mates, Gillies was chasing shadows for the opening ten minutes or so as Monaco moved the ball around with pace, precision and real intent.

Matthis Abline was a real thorn in the side of the Hearts defence and there was an early warning sign when the striker cut them open and teed up a good chance for Takumi Minamino. The former Liverpool winger couldn’t get his shot away, instead scuffing the ball into the path of Diop whose effort was blocked.

It was looking ominous for Hearts at this stage, with Abline quickly surging clear again to set up Christian Mawissa for a shot which flew well over the top, but they gradually secured a foothold in the contest.

Monaco forward Balogun sends the ball beyond Beau Reus to settle a rollercoaster match

Pierre Landry Kabore was first to threaten for the hosts when he muscled his way into the Monaco penalty area but the big striker’s lack of finesse and awareness saw him drag a shot wide when he should have picked out Gillies in a more promising position.

Hearts grew in belief and made the 16th-minute breakthrough with their first wonder strike of the evening. Kerjota’s free-kick from around 20 yards was a decent enough hit, the ball rebounding off Lukas Hradecky’s left hand post.

Claudio Braga did well to keep possession for Hearts and found Altena on the edge of the box. The Dutch full-back displayed outstanding technique to smash a rising shot beyond the helpless Hradecky and send the home fans into raptures.

Monaco briefly appeared rattled and Hearts might have done more to take advantage of a mix-up between Hradecky and Sadibou Sane which saw Laurent Mendy nick the ball and find Kabore who again lacked the composure needed to get a shot on target.

Just as it seemed Hearts were in the ascendancy, however, they gifted Monaco an equaliser. It was another unhappy moment in Europe for Jamie McCart, who scored an own goal in Hearts’ previous game away to Swiss side Thun.

The defender caught Abline with a rash and clumsy challenge inside the box, leaving German referee Daniel Schlager with a simple decision to make as he pointed to the spot.

Jordi Altena turns to celebrate his exquisite opener that sent the Tynecastle crowd wild

Balogun stepped forward and calmly slotted the penalty low to the left of Beau Reus and into the corner of the net.

The goal sparked another spell of dominance from the visitors who were finding it all too easy to pass their way through central midfield where Gillies and Laurent Mendy were regularly outnumbered.

Balogun came close to finding the net again when he got in behind McCart on the left side of the penalty area before dragging a shot just wide from a difficult angle.

The visitors did take the lead in the 41st minute and, once more, Hearts were the architects of their own downfall. This time, they conceded possession cheaply from their own throw-in when Altena took one touch too many and gave the ball away.

Monaco ruthlessly made the most of the opening it presented as Balogun raced clear and set up the unmarked Diop for a simple close-range finish.

No sooner had they seized the initiative, however, Monaco found themselves back on level terms once again as Kerjota conjured up a stunning goal which was arguably even better than Altena’s opener.

Sabah Kerjota unleashes a ridiculous left-footed shot that sailed gracefully into the top corner

Sabri Guendouz, whose pace and direct running was a real headache for Monaco, did well to earn a free-kick on the left. Altena flighted it to the far post where Stuart Findlay won the aerial battle. The ball fell to Kerjota on the right corner of the penalty area and he curled a sumptuous shot beyond Hradecky into the top left corner of the net.

A remarkable first half almost ended with a third Hearts goal in stoppage time. Minamino, already booked, was fortunate to avoid a second yellow card when he tripped Guendouz on the edge of the box. Altena’s set piece expertise was called upon again and he was unlucky to see his dipping effort narrowly clear the crossbar.

Hearts had to defend smartly and bravely for long spells in the second half, no one doing it better than McCart who recovered brilliantly from his earlier setback as he produced several crucial interventions.

Reus had to make fine saves to deny Jordan Teze and Abline but Hearts had menacing moments of their own. Hopes were raised when the ref pointed to the spot for handball against Monaco sub Mathys Detourbet in the 71st minute but the award was rightly reversed by VAR.

Albanian winger Kerjota takes the acclaim of his team-mates before the late heartbreak

Rogers Mato made an astonishing goal-line clearance to prevent Detourbet scoring at the other end and it looked as if Hearts would hold on for a valuable point.

Then came the late, late heartbreak as Mamadou Coulibaly sent Balogun racing free to coolly slot the ball beyond Reus and leave Hearts’ prospects of further progress in the tournament hanging by a thread.

Hearts (4-2-3-1): Reus 7; Altena 7, McCart 7, Findlay 7, Borchgrevink 6 (Mato 46); Gillies 5 (Spittal 46), Mendy 6; Kerjota 8 (Pollock 81), Braga 6 (Wilson 85), Guendouz 7 (McPake 76); Kabore 6. Booked: Altena, Kabore. Manager: Wouter Vrancken 7.

Monaco (3-4-2-1): Hradecky 7; Sane 7, Dier 7, Teze 7; Vanderson 6 (Nazinho 57), Zakaria 6, Diop 6 (Coulibaly 64), Mawissa 6 (Detourbet 64); Minamino 6 (Belmokhtar 57), Abline 8 (Soubeir 87); Balogun 8. Booked: Abline, Minamino, Mawissa, Detourbet. Manager: Filipe Luis 7.

Liverpool are reportedly increasing their interest in Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall, with the Reds enquiring about his availability ahead of a potential transfer next summer.

The England international has established himself as one of the Premier League’s most promising left-backs, but Newcastle’s reluctance to lose him could make negotiations difficult.

According to a TEAMtalk report, Liverpool have enquired about Hall’s situation and want to stay informed about his future at St James’ Park.

The 22-year-old previously attracted considerable interest from Manchester United, but he committed his long-term future to Newcastle in September by signing a new contract until 2031.

The Magpies have no intention of letting their defensive star leave, although sources indicate that an offer exceeding £66 million could bring them to the negotiating table.

Manchester United remain interested in securing his services, meaning Liverpool could face competition from their Premier League rivals if they decide to pursue a deal.

Liverpool are understood to have concerns about Milos Kerkez’s development since his £40 million arrival from Bournemouth in 2025.

The Hungarian international has struggled to deliver consistent performances, prompting the Anfield hierarchy to consider alternatives at left-back.

Hall could be an attractive addition because of his Premier League experience, defensive qualities and ability to contribute going forward. His homegrown status would also make him a valuable acquisition for Liverpool.

However, Newcastle’s determination to retain the defender and his long-term contract make a January transfer unlikely.

Liverpool are expected to continue monitoring his situation, with next summer potentially providing a more realistic opportunity to explore a deal.

Hall remains an important part of Newcastle’s long-term plans, and the Magpies will certainly demand a substantial financial commitment before considering his departure.

#1227. Martin O'Neill praises Colombian goal machine Camilo Duran as he saves the day for Celtic... yet again

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:56 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 18:04 EST, 26 November 2026

Martin O’Neill hailed ‘magnificent’ Camilo Duran for helping Celtic win ugly against Torreense to keep their Europa League dream alive.

The Parkhead men looked to be in for a rare comfortable night on the road when Torreense defender Javi Vazquez scored an own goal after nine minutes.

But sloppy defending by the visitors allowed the Portuguese to level 10 minutes later through Dany Jean.

With the minnows sitting in and hoping for a point late on, though, veteran James Forrest climbed off the bench to set up fellow sub Duran for his 15th goal of the season.

On the late impact of the Colombian, O’Neill said: ‘I think you always have to keep the faith. But we were gambling almost everything. They were camped outside their penalty area and we were hoping at some stage or another somebody might come up with something.

‘And of course, once again, Duran has done it. He is just a magnificent footballer.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill praised Camilo Duran for once again riding to the rescue

‘Fifteen goals and we’re not into December yet. He’s been flying, he’s a terrific player, there’s no question about it.

‘That’s two games he’s come up big for us as well (on back of Besiktas). Maybe 22 games, in all honesty. But he’s been great. He didn’t start the game although we knew he could come on.’

Although delighted with the result, O’Neill was the first to admit that the performance was not all it might have been.

‘Despite the fact that we’d plenty of possession, I thought that we should just accelerate once or twice, not only just into their half, but also be more penetrative,’ he added.

‘And I think that was the point. I thought we had a lot of ball in the second half as well.

‘There’s always a possibility on the break that you could concede but we had to take the chance because the three points tonight were of vital importance.

‘But, yeah, there’s lots that we can still do to improve our game.’

Duran's downward header sealed the points for Celtic and ignited their qualification hopes

The dramatic outcome ensured Celtic are now up to 25th place in the 36-team group – from 32nd – after losing their opening three matches.

O’Neill’s men next face Omonia with Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise to come in January.

‘I’m just delighted to have won — it keeps us going,’ added O’Neill. ‘We’ve got six points on the board and we’ve still got a couple of games to go.

‘So, from an absolutely almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we’ve given ourselves some hope.’

Celtic’s star man on the night, Jota set up the opening goal and relished the return to his homeland almost two years after his last European match.

‘It’s been a long time that I wanted to come back to Portugal and play in front of my friends and family,’ he said. ‘And there’s no better way than with a win with three points. It was something that we wanted to achieve today and luckily we did it.

‘It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible. And right now it’s all about enjoying. There’s no expectation — just to be a professional, having the responsibility of being a Celtic player and delivering every day.’

#1226. Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has quickly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

They kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

Treatment is needed for Zubimendi after he is caught on the nose by Barry.

Big chance for Everton. Garner whips a teasing cross into the box, Dewsbury-Hall meets it with his head on the run but the ball flies just wide of the post.

EvertonOFF Johnson, Mykolenko ON Dibling, Hackney

Tarkowski is the latest yellow card for Everton after a foul on Havertz.

Eze with a poor cross into the box. He fails to run back quickly and Arteta sprints to the edge of the touchline and goes berserk at the midfielder.

How have Arsenal reacted to their top scorer Saka being injured? Both of their centre backs have scored for the first time this season.

On his 200 Premier League appearance for Arsenal, Gabriel marks it with his first goal of the season.

It is a lovely move with slick one-touch passing. The ball is fed to White making a run down the outside and he clips the ball to the far post for Gabriel to head home.

OFF Merino, Lewis-Skelly, GyokeresON Calafiori, Guimaraes, Havertz

Garner is booked for Everton now after barging into Merino off the ball.

Arteta is shown a yellow card for something. Not sure what for yet. But the Arsenal manager is looking to make some changes off the bench.

Arsenal have been guilty of overplaying today. Opting for the extra pass rather than taking a shot. The game is open at the moment and that makes things dangerous for the home side.

Yellow card for Lewis-Skelly after bringing down Johnson. Gabriel is back on the pitch and seems happy enough to continue.

Arsenal have defensive options in Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori and Mosquera if Arteta wants to avoid taking any risks.

A worry for Arsenal as Gabriel jars his knee into the ground as he tries to clear the ball. The Brazilian is receiving treatment and hobbles off the pitch.

Gabriel immediately raised his hand for medical attention after making that clearance. He really extended his leg to get the ball away. Looks to be in a lot of pain.

Latest corner from Arsenal after Eze’s shot is blocked by Rohl. Rice’s delivery into the near post is headed clear to Odegaard, who shoots ambitiously from distance and Pickford collects the ball comfortably.

Arsenal get the match restarted. The longer the match goes on without extending the lead, Everton will think they have a chance.

Before today, Arsenal had averaged five corners per match in the Premier League this season. In the first 45 minutes here, they had 10 corners.

Yellow card for Mykolenko after he catches White wide on the right. Rice whips the ball in and Merino meets it with a flick goalwards but the ball goes over the bar.

That is the final touch of the half and the players are running off to get dry!

Big chance for Everton. White thinks he has time when he heads the ball back to Raya but he does not connect well and Barry is there to pick it up and he flicks a shot at goal but Raya reacts quickly to parry the ball.

Raya is penalised for taking too long with the ball and Everton have a cheap corner. Danger is cleared by Arsenal as they force Everton back into their half.

The conditions are terrible at the moment. Heavy wind and rain causing havoc.

A lot of set-pieces for Arsenal today as they continue to put Everton under the cosh. Can they take advantage of their dominance again before the break?

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Another effort at goal for Madueke. This one is a snapshot from the edge of the box that goes into the side netting.

Madueke should do better. Rice finds him and the winger drives into the box. He takes a shot but drags a right-footed effort wide.

Chance for Arsenal. Rice finds space behind the Everton midfield and drives forward. He plays a pass to Lewis-Skelly, who lays it off to Eze. The England midfielder sidefoots a cross into the box but no one in an Arsenal shirt is there to meet it.

Courtesy of Opta: Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal in all competitions (not including penalties) since May of last season against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.

George is looking lively for Everton. He tries to come inside and whip an effort to the far corner but the ball deflects wide.

From the corner, Gabriel clears off the line after Raya loses track of the ball.

Everton have responded impressively to the Konsa goal and have been the better team since falling behind. Midfielders Garner and Armstrong are growing into the game quite nicely.

Everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any plans to sit deep and play on the counter.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

“They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

This is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”

This is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

Chelsea are reportedly in a race with Brighton and Barcelona to sign Argentine wonderkid Simon Escobar, with the 17-year-old defender attracting growing interest after impressive performances for club and country.

The Velez Sarsfield youngster has emerged as one of South America’s most promising defensive prospects, with his versatility and attacking qualities making him an attractive option for several European clubs.

According to a TEAMtalk report, Chelsea and Brighton have continued to monitor the teenager after initially identifying him as a potential long-term addition earlier this year.

Barcelona have also entered the picture, with the Spanish giants keeping tabs on his development as they look to strengthen their defensive options with emerging young talent.

Escobar has already gained valuable first-team experience in Argentina’s top flight and further enhanced his reputation with some impressive displays for the national under-17 side.

The left-back has also captained Argentina at the Under-17 World Cup, scoring important goals during the competition and demonstrating his leadership qualities.

Velez have recognised his growing reputation by extending his contract until December 2028, strengthening their negotiating position ahead of potential approaches from Europe.

Despite growing interest, an immediate transfer is unlikely, as FIFA regulations prevent the youngster from moving to Europe until he turns 18 next summer.

Velez are also under no pressure to sanction his departure, viewing the teenager as an important part of their plans for the coming seasons.

Chelsea and Brighton are therefore expected to continue assessing his progress rather than rushing into an immediate transfer agreement.

The youngster’s ability to operate further forward, carry possession and contribute offensively could make him an exciting addition to either Premier League side.

However, Barcelona’s involvement could complicate matters for the English clubs, particularly given their reputation for developing talented youngsters.

Escobar still has considerable development ahead of him, but his performances have already attracted attention from some of Europe’s biggest clubs. A strong campaign could further increase competition for his signature next summer.

#1223. Just eight universities dominate Nobel and other top economics prizes

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Sarah Wild is a freelance journalist in Canterbury, UK.

Researchers from Harvard and seven other US universities including MIT, Princeton and Yale, dominate economics prizes.Credit: Jade Gao/AFP via Getty

Major prizes in economics, including the Nobel are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities, according to a working paper published last month1.

Eight institutions dominate the world's top economics prizes, led Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

This contrasts with prizes awarded in disciplines in the natural sciences, engineering and social sciences outside economics. These have become less concentrated among certain instituions over the past 70 years, according to the working paper, which has not yet been peer reviewed.

“The whole world now does science,” says Richard Freeman, an economist at Harvard University and an author on the paper, which is an update to an article presented at a National Bureau of Economic Research Summer Institute workshop in a 20242. “Our initial thought was that as the science spreads out, so too should all the prizes.” And that was the case — except in economics where “it went the other direction”.

Economist John Hassler, who is based at Stockholm University and chairs the prize-awarding committee for the Economics Prize in Memory of Alfred Nobel, says that the overall finding of concentration among a small group of US universities is not a complete surprise.

“The trend is truly eye-opening and adds another dimension to the understanding of inequality within the economics profession,” adds Ashwini Deshpande, an economist at Ashoka University in Sonipat, India. “The low levels of gender, ethnic and geographic diversity within authors of top journal papers and prizes is well known and a matter of concern.”

Freeman and his colleagues examined 171 different awards and focused their analyses on those given between 1960 and 2022, including Nobel prizes (except for literature and peace), the Fields Medal for mathematics and the Breakthrough science prizes established in 2012 by the founders of technology companies among others.

The authors of the working paper analysed the academic affiliations of the 5,859 prizewinners, working out the number of years they were linked to a specific institution. They call this metric ‘affiliation years’.

Of the 18 scientific fields of the prizewinners, 17 had a greater variety of universities represented among recipients over the time period. Economics was the outlier.

Among winners of the economics Nobel prize, seven out of 148 institutions made up 50% of affiliation years. It means that, of all the years that economics Nobel prizewinners dedicated to their discipline in academia, half of them were spent in the seven institutions.

For chemistry Nobels, 23 institutions out of 216 accounted for half of affiliation years. Twenty-six out of 243 institutions accounted for 50% of affiliation years for the physiology or medicine Nobel, and 17 out of 200 for the physics prize.

When the authors assessed all the main economics prizes between 1960 and 2022 (not only the Nobel), they found that researchers from eight out of 249 institutions represented 50% of affiliation years. In addition to Harvard, the eight are: the University of Chicago in Illinois; Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Cambridge; Stanford University in California; Princeton University in New Jersey; Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut; the University of California, Berkeley; and Columbia University in New York.

By contrast, for assessed prizes in the natural sciences, 37 institutions out of 1,318 account for 50% of affiliation-years as of 2022; for engineering prizes it is 27 out of 783; and for social sciences prizes (minus economics), it is 23 out of 744. Unlike in economics, the trend for these fields is towards less concentration (see ‘Spot the outlier’).

The authors propose some possible explanations. One of these relates to another finding of the paper: “The institutions producing most of the field’s recognized work also establish the toolkit that the rest of the fields adopts,” the paper’s authors say. “Work using an unfamiliar approach is hard to place or recognize, and findings that disagree with the main tenets of the field are rejected rather than studied as special cases that may yield new knowledge.”

Another factor, they report is that in economics, 55 per cent of Nobel laureates received the prize for a broad body of work. This contrasts somewhat with medicine and the other sciences. Some 50 per cent of prize winners in chemistry, 59 per cent in physics and 70 per cent in medicine were awarded for testable findings.

Hanzhang Zhou, a co-author on the paper and an economics doctoral candidate at MIT, says: “When you’re giving the prize for somebody’s lifetime agenda, the institution that they’re associated with is usually one of the factors that you do take into account,” she explains.

Hassler told Nature that the economics prize is not intended to be a lifetime achievement award and follows the rules governing the other prize categories. He says it is a prize for a well-defined contribution or breakthrough, should also lead to further research in the field and that the finding must also have relevance to society at large.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03333-3

Freeman, R. B., Xie, D., Zhang, H. & Zhou, H. NBER Working Paper 35875 (National Bureau of Economic Research, 2026).

Freeman, R. B., Xie, D., Zhang, H. & Zhou, H. in NBER Summer Institute – The Science of Science Funding https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f204525.pdf (2024).

Arsenal are reportedly not pursuing a move for Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs, despite being linked with the Portuguese international ahead of the January transfer window.

The 22-year-old has enjoyed an impressive campaign in Belgium, attracting attention from several Premier League clubs following his outstanding performances for the Belgian champions.

According to a TEAMtalk report, Arsenal are not currently considering a move for Forbs, despite their recruitment staff being aware of his progress.

The Gunners have reportedly sent scouts to watch Club Brugge on several occasions this season, including their recent Champions League encounter against Liverpool.

However, those scouting missions have focused primarily on another attacking talent, Nicolo Tresoldi, rather than the Portuguese winger.

Forbs has established himself as an important figure at Brugge since joining from Ajax in the summer of 2025. He has registered five goals and eight assists in 17 appearances across all competitions this season, earning his first senior international call-ups with Portugal.

His impressive performances have also attracted interest from Aston Villa and Newcastle United, with both Premier League clubs continuing to monitor his development.

Arsenal’s decision to stay away from Forbs is understandable, considering their existing options in wide attacking positions.

Mikel Arteta already has considerable depth on the flanks, and the club’s recruitment strategy appears to be focused on strengthening other areas of the squad.

Tresoldi has emerged as a more prominent target following his impressive performances for Brugge. The young striker has scored five Champions League goals this season, including a remarkable hat-trick against Inter Milan.

Arsenal could consider bringing in another centre-forward during the January transfer window if a suitable opportunity emerges.

Such an addition could also have implications for Viktor Gyokeres, whose future may come under scrutiny if the Gunners decide to strengthen their attacking department.

For now, Forbs is not understood to be part of Arsenal’s immediate recruitment plans.

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, said.

“We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”

Leicester were buoyed in the week by re-signing Jack van Poortfliet, who extended his contract with his boyhood club.

I grew up supporting Leicester, it’s always been my club,” said the England scrum half. This place feels like home in my rugby life. The club is in a really good position, I think we have a great group of lads and great coaches.

I love playing rugby here, I have my best mates here and I believe that we’ve got a group of lads that we can do great things with. I want to be in a place that I love playing for and I believe can win trophies.”

Squally conditions this afternoon at Mattioli Welford Road - in fact make that horrible. An interesting test then for Northampton as lovers of the beautiful game.

You would imagine that the rain and wind would suit a Leicester side whose DNA is set piece power better.

Expect the catch and drive to get plenty of game time and Jack van Poortvliet and Billy Searle to go to the air regularly. It could be a stern examination for teenage Saints full-back James Pater.

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

#1220. Flamengo director confirms minimum price tag for Roma-linked Samuel Lino

Flamengo director José Boto insists the Brazilian club will sell Roma-linked Samuel Lino only for a ‘very high offer’ but refuses to confirm Giallorossi interest.

Several sources report that Flamengo wing-back Samuel Lino is on Roma’s shopping list. Earlier this week, RTI Esporte even claimed that the Giallorossi were ready to submit a €45m bid for the 26-year-old.

“Several clubs are interested, but I won’t say whether Roma is among them,” Flamengo director Boto told TMW.

“I can confirm that the interest in him is concrete, and we receive inquiries about the player every day. We bought Lino at a favourable age for a possible future sale. We paid €25m for him, and obviously we won’t sell him for less. I don’t even know if we’ll sell him at all, unless we receive a very high offer.”

Samuel Lino joined Flamengo from Atletico Madrid in the summer of 2025.

The Brazil international has scored 13 goals and provided nine assists in 35 appearances in the Brazilian Serie A this season.

Roma already did business with Flamengo in recent years, signing Brazilian full-back Wesley for €25m plus add-ons in 2025. The Brazilian club used the proceeds from Wesley’s sale to sign Samuel Lino from Atletico Madrid.

Roma sit second in the Serie A table with 30 points from 12 matches and are the only unbeaten team, alongside their city rivals Lazio, who lead the table.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.
