#1219. Torreense 1-2 Celtic: Camilo Duran springs from the bench to get Bhoys out of jail again

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:40 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 18:11 EST, 26 November 2026

Some 90 miles north of the scene of the club’s crowning moment, Celtic ensured that their latest return to Portugal did not tarnish the legacy of the Lisbon Lions.

Sleep would not have come easily to Martin O’Neill ahead of this awkward assignment in the small city of Leiria.

Almost 60 years ago, the Northern Irishman watched Jock Stein’s legendary side defeat Inter Milan on a black-and-white television while in boarding school.

For the current side to fail to see off a second division side in Torreense would have been embarrassing enough at the best of times. For it to have happened in this season of all seasons would have added to the sense of shame.

In a game where a victory was really the only acceptable outcome, O’Neill’s men toiled for the longest time yet got there in the end.

Yet again, Camilo Duran was the toast of the visiting supporters as he claimed his 15th goal of the season with six minutes remaining.

Celtic's performance certainly wasn’t pretty. But after a diabolical start to this Europa League campaign, the Parkhead men are back in the saddle.

Camilo Duran celebrates after his 84th minute header saved Celtic's skins in Portugal

Now with back-to-back victories against Besiktas and Torreense, O’Neill’s men have more than a puncher’s chance of reaching the play-off round again.

One win from their remaining games with Omonia, Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise might get them there. Four points certainly will. It goes without saying, however, that they will have to produce much better than they did here.

After a tough six-week spell when the team looked lost, though, O’Neill has taken it to a better place. For just the third time this season, Celtic have chalked up four straight wins.

Although O’Neill had stressed that he still wanted to make an appreciable impact on Europe, there was an air of compromise about his line-up ahead of Sunday’s trip to Tynecastle.

Duran was initially stationed on the bench with Kasper Hogh, no goals in his past 16 games, tasked with leading the line. It’s fair to say the Dane did not enhance his reputation.

With Cameron Carter-Vickers nursing a strain, Dane Murray was stripped although the pair were swapped at the interval.

Jota, unsurprisingly, started in his homeland after being drafted into the squad as a replacement for the injured Mika Baur. By some distance, the winger was Celtic’s best player on the night.

The Colombian heads the ball home after a superb cross by fellow sub James Forrest

Built for Euro 2004, the Estadio Dr Magalhaes Pessoa in Leiria made for a strange backdrop to a match of such significance.

With Torreense forced by UEFA to play 60 miles from their own tiny ground, Celtic supporters outnumbered the Portuguese fans by two-to-one.

The fast start would have met with O’Neill’s approval. Liam Scales flicked on a corner which Adriel, Torreense’s Brazilian keeper, flapped at. Yang Hyun-jun’s goal-bound shot was blocked.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain then played a measured pass down the left to release Jota. The cross was attacked by Yang, but knocked clear. Amid the chaos, Hogh took a boot to the head which required treatment.

Jota was already relishing the task of tormenting Jonathan Mutombo. When he faced the right-back up on nine minutes, he eased past him in a blur of skill and pace.

The cross which followed was menacing. Stood at the far post, Javi Vazquez, under pressure from Yang, tried to usher the ball round the post and got it all wrong. He lashed the ball into his own net. Celtic had the early breakthrough they craved so badly.

It's relief for Martin O'Neill after Duran sprung from the bench to seal a 2-1 victory

With Torreense then compelled to come out, everything was in Celtic’s favour. Provided they maintained the tempo of the match and their quality on the ball, it had the makings of a comfortable night. So much for that theory.

For reasons only they could explain, Celtic became sloppy with the ball and lethargic without it.

Torreense served a warning that the game wasn’t done when Sam Johnstone had to boot away a free-kick. It wasn’t heeded.

Arriving on 19 minutes, the nature of the leveller was shocking from O’Neill’s perspective. Alex Alfaro was given far too much time on the edge of the box to take aim and fire. The ball bounced back off the bar.

Kieran Tierney panicked and sliced a clearance. As Dany Jean pounced, Colby Donovan put in a half-hearted tackle. The Haiti international smashed the ball home from an angle.

Could Celtic quickly respond? Not if they were depending on Hogh. The Dane earned a break of the ball and couldn’t pick out Jota.

Hogh’s ball retention started to go from bad to worse. Yang, who’d begun the game brightly, was equally as culpable of that failing.

Time and again Celtic looked to Jota to provide a moment of magic. He danced away from Manu Pozo on the flank and fired a rocket towards goal. Adriel beat it away.

Another terrific delivery from the winger presented Hogh with another chance to end his goal drought. Again, he lacked any conviction and the keeper made a routine save.

Camilo Duran goes over to celebrate in front of the fans who made the trip to Portugal

Torreense were not without their moments. Scales was forced to clear the ball off the line after Volnei Feltes had enjoyed a free header following a foul.

Hogh did well to pick the pocket of Stopira in the right channel. The Cape Verde international breathed a sigh of relief as the forward again failed to steer the ball away from Adriel’s arms as a raft of visiting players were poised to claim a tap-in.

Another excellent delivery from Jota saw Luke McCowan win the ball at the back post. On this occasion, it was hard to fault Hogh for not connecting with the headed ball back across goal.

The second half simply had to be much better from Celtic. Jota was gifted a chance to claim a second when Stopira passed the ball straight to him. His chip didn’t have quite enough to beat the keeper.

Jota dribbled his way to the line and centred. Oxlade-Chamberlain let the ball run to Tierney. The full-back lashed a shot which Feltes stood up tall to block.

Donovan’s weak strike was the cue for O’Neill to ring the changes, with Duran and Oliver Sorensen replacing Hogh and Oxlade-Chamberlain.

Before either substitute had enjoyed a touch of the ball, the impressive Jean fired into Johnstone’s side-net. This was not going to plan.

Duran is hailed by team-mates Donovan and Forrest after his late rescue act for Celtic

O’Neill’s men were mighty fortunate not to fall behind with 20 minutes left. Scales completely misjudged a long ball. Carter-Vickers didn’t provide cover. Musa Drammeh, the former Hearts forward, ought to have done better to fire his shot beyond the far post.

With Jota off after tiring, it all got rather desperate. Within the space of 60 seconds, Yang let a simple pass roll under his foot before Sorensen ran the ball out of play.

It was to be a combination of an old stager and the man of the moment which saved the day, however.

With six minutes remaining, substitute James Forrest bobbed and weaved his way down the right and sent in a cross which you’d seen a thousand times. Duran attacked it and thumped home a clinical header.

Played in by Forrest, McCowan was prevented from claiming a late third by the keeper’s legs. Relief was the overriding emotion at the end.

#1217. Gattuso: Taylor ruled out of Torino clash, but Lazio ‘can’t settle for what we have’

Lazio coach Gennaro Gattuso says Kenneth Taylor will miss tomorrow’s game against Torino, but he has faith in Fisayo Dele-Bashiru: ‘We can’t settle for what we have. Inter have more points than they did at this stage last year, and that tells you a lot.’

Serie A table leaders Lazio visit Torino tomorrow, but the Biancocelesti will be forced to cope without Dutch midfielder Taylor.

“Taylor won’t be available. He had a problem in the second half against Lecce,” Gattuso said at a press conference via TMW.

“He’s had an MRI scan that showed some swelling, and he’ll have another on Monday; Tavares, Sutalo, and Marusic will as well. He won’t be available for the match, while the others, including Noslin and Zaccagni, are doing well.

“The system won’t change; we’ll continue on our pathway. We might pay a price in terms of build-up, but tomorrow’s game fits well with our characteristics,” Gattuso added.

“Nobody can give us what Taylor does, but we’ll do what we know. We’ll put in something more in terms of pace and physicality.”

The Lazio coach seems to have already picked a replacement for Taylor.

“I want to be honest. Dele-Bashiru deserved much more [playing time], and it’s only fair that he sometimes put on an angry face,” he said.

“I make decisions, but he’s improved and has qualities that fit the game. He must play without pressure and show his technical and physical qualities.

“We know the team we’ll face tomorrow. Second balls and transitions will be crucial.”

Tomorrow’s game will be a reunion between Gattuso and his ex-Milan teammate Ignazio Abate.

“I’m happy with what Ignazio is doing; I put him under my protective wing since he was a kid. I’m on really good terms with him. We Milan veterans left something in the young players, and I’m proud of it. He was a teammate, and I coached him too,” Gattuso said.

“I even played him at centre-back, and he’d leave San Siro to applause from the fans. To see where he is now and how he is growing as a coach makes me proud because I have great memories of him.”

Lazio are the Serie A table leaders and the only unbeaten team in the league alongside city rivals Roma.

“I hope to stay for as long as possible, but ultimately, what happens on the pitch will decide. It’s reductive to talk about the standings. I had a coach, Allegri, who is phenomenal with the numbers, whereas I’m not very good with them. I take things day by day, so all I know is that tomorrow we’re going into a difficult match where we need to improve our position in the table,” Gattuso said.

“We win, but the others win too. There’s a gap in the standings, and we can’t afford to make mistakes. I keep an eye on the table because when you’re having a season like this and the others keep getting results, you’re always right there

“It’s great to be up there with Roma; for Lazio and Roma fans, it’s something incredible. But right now, we just have to focus on improving our position—we can’t settle for what we have. Inter have more points than they did at this stage last year, and that tells you a lot.”

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

#1215. Pascal Gross interview: Brighton isn't a nice stepping stone club anymore. We're a big club who need to be ruthless - we can win every game

Published: 21:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 26 November 2026

Before Pascal Gross returned for his second spell at Brighton last January, he sat down for a rather frank conversation with manager Fabian Hurzeler. It was time, he suggested, for the club to take the next step.

‘There were some games in the past where we went (away to big teams) and you're not sure you can really do it,’ Gross tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘But we should now have a mindset that we can win every game. I really believe in that. We have the players. That’s what I said.

‘People say we are nice club and, yeah, maybe we are. But on the pitch, it was time to be ruthless. Time to kill games, be a big club. That’s what this is about now.’

Gross may feel his ambition has been vindicated, at least in part. Brighton sit second in the Premier League table, despite a disappointment at Hull last weekend that saw them lose a game they had dominated at the death. Gross, 35, ended that one on his knees in his own penalty area, having tried in vain to stop Oli McBurnie sliding in Hull’s second goal.

‘That felt really, really bad,’ he says. ‘Maybe today (Tuesday) is the first day I am starting to feel a bit better about it. I would be more worried if we didn’t create chances. We did. We just didn’t score.’

‘On the pitch, it was time to be ruthless,' Pascal Gross tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Time to kill games, be a big club. That’s what this is about now’

Brighton sit second in the Premier League table, despite a disappointment at Hull last weekend that saw them lose a game they had dominated at the death

Before Gross returned for his second spell at Brighton last January, he sat down for a rather frank conversation with manager Fabian Hurzeler

Brighton are six points behind leaders Arsenal – who they have already beaten 3-0 at the Amex – but are the Premier League’s top scorers by a distance, with 26.

Gross, the German who returned to Sussex after a short spell at Borussia Dortmund, has created an astonishing 31 chances for his team. That puts him only two behind the best in the country this term, his friend and Germany team-mate Florian Wirtz.

The debate about Wirtz’s value or otherwise to Liverpool has swirled around the country since he arrived at Liverpool in the summer of 2025 for £116million. The conversation even reached Brighton’s training ground.

‘Jamie Redknapp was there and he asked me all about it just a couple weeks ago,’ Gross explains. ‘I just told him: "He's too good not to prove himself." People here still don't know how good he is, but they will. He's a complete package and he knows I support him a lot.

‘Football is a team sport. It’s not ever on one person. Also, nobody should forget just how difficult and different the Premier League is when you first come.’

Gross knows this well. He smiles at the mention of his own first English away game – a 2-0 defeat at Leicester in August 2017 that brings to mind the Patrice Evra quote about his first experience of playing in England being akin to ‘an afternoon spent in a washing machine’.

‘I was on the floor so much that day that I looked like a little child,’ Gross recalls. ‘It was just all too physical. I knew I had to improve fast, play faster. My decision-making had to be quicker.

‘My father called me after and said I wouldn’t last three weeks if I played like that again. But I already knew. Going home that day, I really questioned a lot of things. But that’s just how hard it is when you come to the Premier League.’

Gross had a brutal introduction to the Premier League in 2017, but it was a reminder of the level he needed to reach

Gross fires in Brighton's equaliser at Old Trafford in the Carabao Cup back in September. The Seagulls trailed 2-0 but fought back brilliantly to dump out Man United

Brighton players Luka Vuskovic and Groß visit local independent restaurant Riddle & Finns to support American Express' Shop Small campaign

The Hull game was Gross' 300th in a Brighton shirt, and he is perhaps playing at a higher level than ever with four goals and four assists in the first 11 league games this season, as well as a goal in the Carabao Cup win at Manchester United. On an official club podcast, former striker and team-mate Glenn Murray labelled him Brighton's best-ever player, and last week he signed a new contract keeping him on the south coast until the end of next season.

Signed by Chris Hughton from Bundesliga side Ingolstadt after the Seagulls' promotion to the top division a little over nine years ago, Gross has had an inside view of the most successful period in the club’s history.

During his time, Brighton have sold enough players for big profit to make a pretty good Premier League XI – Robert Sanchez, Ben White, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marc Cucurella, Moises Caicedo, Alexis Mac Allister, Leandro Trossard and Joao Pedro get you most of the way there, for a total transfer taking of £424m. Gross suspects there will be more over time.

Equally, he feels the days of players using Brighton as a stepping stone to the next level are gone. A lack of commitment soon gets sniffed out, he says.

‘There have been players who saw it like that,’ he explains. ‘And they couldn't even get in our team because they came with the wrong mindset. If you don't have the right mentality, you don't want to work every day, you can't get in the Brighton team.

‘And if you do come with the right mentality and you push every day, and the team is doing well, I always say that good things will come for everybody – for the club, for the coaches, for the players.

‘I love the club, and we have big potential. There will always be players that move on. But I think the players who come here now, they know we are bigger than a jumping club. We're a big club in the Premier League. We have been there almost 10 years and are improving all the time.’

Gross thought hard before first leaving Germany for England. He visited Brighton’s training ground twice before making his decision and, once he had, dug down into the individual statistics of the players who would soon be team-mates.

Gross (right) has seen a huge change at Brighton since joining from Bundesliga side Ingolstadt, where he played under former Southampton manager Ralph Hasenhuttl (left)

Brighton's form this season has been inspired by a prolific attack, with their 26 Premier League goals by far the most in the division

They have progressed season on season despite the departure of a host of star players for big money, including Alexis Mac Allister (right) to Liverpool for £35m in 2023

Having married and had two children in Sussex, Gross has the club in his heart and soul now. We meet to talk at beachfront restaurant Riddle & Finns as part of American Express’s Shop Small campaign, encouraging people to support local business.

During his spell at Dortmund – who he adored as a boy – Gross watched every Brighton game on TV. But it may not have been this way. There was a time, in pre-season 2020, when former Brighton manager Graham Potter told Gross he could leave.

‘That was hard to take,’ Gross says. ‘I asked him if there was no chance at all of me playing. I needed to know if he saw me as, like, No17 or 18 in the squad so that whatever I did, I wouldn't play. Or in his mind was I 12, 13 or 14?

‘Then I figured I could work my way back into the team because I would always back myself to prove the manager wrong. We lost a lot of games and eventually, I came back into the team.’

Gross’s approach back then was to train as well and as hard as he could. Murray recalls that his attitude stood out.

‘It wasn’t my team-mates’ fault I wasn’t playing,’ explains Gross. ‘Why would I take it out on them? That wouldn’t make sense.’

Culture is often discussed in modern football but it’s just a new word for an old truth: unhappy football teams tend to fail.

‘There are days when you see, maybe, that the way we play gives an opponent frustration and you can see bad body language,’ Gross says. ‘That's where I sense we have them.

‘It wasn’t my team-mates’ fault I wasn’t playing,’ explains Gross, pictured celebrating the win at Man City with Jack Hinshelwood. ‘Why would I take it out on them? That wouldn’t make sense’

'If you don't have the right mentality, you don't want to work every day, you can't get in the Brighton team'

'Players who come here now, they know we are bigger than a jumping club. We're a big club in the Premier League'

‘But there are also teams who maybe struggle but they are still together and they're still fighting and you see a group of guys who can still be hard to beat. That’s about culture. It’s important and I think we value that here.’

As part of Brighton’s leadership group, Gross speaks regularly to manager and compatriot Hurzeler. His personal creed is that confidence should never bleed into arrogance – ‘I just hate that’ – and he believes that Hurzeler, known to rub the occasional manager up the wrong way, is on the right side of the line.

‘He is pushing, pushing,’ Gross says with a smile. ‘He has so much passion for the job, he puts so much work into it. He wants to challenge, he wants to think differently.

‘He doesn't want to think: “Everything is nice." He really wants to push himself and us. And that balance is a really fine balance. He's trying to stretch the limit and I think that's good.’

Pascal Gross is supporting American Express Shop Small, which aims to support small businesses by encouraging the nation to back their local high street on Small Business Saturday and beyond. This year, American Express is investing £1million in new Shop Small grants, offering 100 independent UK businesses £10,000 each to help them grow, innovate and invest in their future. Visit go.amex/shopsmalluk

#1213. ‘If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?’: mathematicians shocked and excited by AI breakthroughs

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Mathematics Álvaro Lozano-Robledo thought the Riemann hypothesis was out of AI’s reach for now.Credit: Bri Diaz/UConn Photo

The news came on a Friday — and it was ground-shaking. For months, reports have mounted of artificial-intelligence models toppling some of the toughest problems in mathematics, plunging the field into turmoil. But the latest claim was the most shocking yet: an AI model had helped to solve the field’s most famous open problem, the Riemann hypothesis.

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

The proof was released on 20 November by mathematician Levent Alpöge at AI giant Anthropic in San Francisco, California, who used an advanced version of the firm’s Claude model. It came in the form of 17 million lines of code in the open-source programming language Lean, which translates mathematical arguments into computer-certifiable code. In a matter of hours, a separate set of mathematicians rushed out a human-written proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which is in the branch of number theory and pertains to the randomness of prime numbers.

Alpöge’s proof has been independently verified by the non-profit organization behind Lean and the Mathlib Initiative, which runs the reference library of formalized mathematics results written in Lean. “We have full confidence that Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him,” the community said in a statement on 21 November.

The mathematics community has broadly accepted the claim, although responses differ wildly. Some celebrate Alpöge’s achievement, but others see the development as proof that humans are fighting against machines for the future of mathematics.

Nature hears reactions from five mathematicians on what solving the Riemann hypothesis means to them.

Mathematician Tasmin Chu is part of the Association for Human Mathematics, whose members commit to doing AI-free research.Credit: Elizabeth Xiao

Tasmin Chu, PhD student in mathematics at the California Institute of Technology in Pasadena.

A technology that can autonomously prove the Riemann hypothesis is no trivial matter. I think that it is imperative our society acts to pause AI development as soon as possible. Over the past year, mathematical institutions have faced the impossible task of adapting to the rapidly changing capabilities of AI in real time.

It’s enormously disruptive for early-career researchers — the people who are the intellectual future of our field. Soon other sectors of society will face the same issues.

My reaction is grave concern. AI companies urgently require democratic oversight. I do not think AI’s encroachment into math is inevitable, nor is the death of human mathematical practice inevitable. It’s a choice to disempower ourselves, just as it’s a choice to continue building these technologies despite grave safety concerns. I continue to practice mathematics without LLMs, because I believe it’s critical that scientific inquiry continues in the hands of human beings. Some of us at the Association for Human Mathematics — whose organizing committee I am on — are collectively making the same decision.

Harini Desiraju, lecturer in mathematics at the University of Warwick, UK.

Given the events of the past few months, this news wasn't entirely a surprise, but we need to wait to understand the Lean proof and let the experts verify it. It is several million lines of code, after all.

I am not a number theorist, so I might not have the same emotional attachment to the Riemann hypothesis. Nevertheless, I have deep appreciation for the ubiquity and the importance of the problem in several areas of maths and physics.

As for the recent events, I want to distinguish between formal proofs versus knowledge. It is an impressive feat to solve such a problem. However, because it is a Lean proof over millions of lines, it is going to take a while before the community gets real understanding, and validity of the proof. With an AI-independent approach available as well, it could present a great opportunity for discovery of new ideas and mathematics. We need to see how it all plays out.

There is another discussion to be had, which involves the role of frontier labs in research. Most of us see the potential benefits of this technology, but it is of utmost importance that we work towards a future where the agency is with the scientific community and not a couple of companies.

Mathematician Marcus Du Sautoy is anxious about what’s next for his field.Credit: David Levenson/Getty

Marcus Du Sautoy, mathematician and professor for the public understanding of science at the University of Oxford, UK.

It was real mix of emotions. A part of me says, how exciting to be alive when this great problem was solved! I think even when Fermat’s last theorem was solved, we had the same excitement and the same melancholy: that great motivator is gone.

Mixed in with that, is the complete surprise that it ended up being proved this way. If you’d asked me three months ago, I would never have predicted it.

There’s quite a lot of anxiety about what ‘math 2.0’ is going to look like.

Xin Zhang, assistant professor in mathematics at the University of Hong Kong.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03835-0

#1212. Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had said he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

In between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX

A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

"Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz

Tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

Tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. The Frenchman played a one-two with Andy Robertson and the Scotsman picked out Marmoush with a low cross. But, six yards out and with time to pick his spot, the former Manchester City man allowed Penders to make a save.

The missed Marmoush chance was the first time Penders had been called into action. At the other end, Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made unnecessary work for himself.

Kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

Neto was Chelsea’s most dangerous player, but it was the wrong call by Alonso to leave Danny Welbeck on the bench, with João Pedro out injured, and he was too slow to change things. Leaving it until the 88th minute, when the game had already been killed by Tel, to send on the striker was a clear error.

Storm Boelo created wet-and-wild conditions on the Stamford Bridge pitch, while there were still remnants of Storm Austen, or should that be Storm Austin, on the home bench.

Chelsea set-piece coach Austin MacPhee let out an incredibly loud “for f---’s sake” when one corner routine went wrong. Nobody could hear what he was shouting over the Tottenham celebrations when Penders scored his own goal, but it would almost certainly have started with “f” again.

James Maddison had been a doubt before the game after missing training during the week and it only took four minutes of the second half for him to signal to De Zerbi that he needed to come off.

Maddison had scored a brilliant goal on his first league start in 18 months against Coventry, but he had to be replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Gallagher at Stamford Bridge.

James Maddison is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Conor Gallagher, who receives a mixed reception from his former fans 🔃 https://t.co/GSeXQQ3eoa

The Chelsea fans predictably booed Gallagher, a graduate of the club’s academy who at times even stood in as captain. The foul on Gallagher that earned Palmer his marching orders silenced the jeers and the Chelsea fans’ boos only returned at the final whistle for their own players.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

#1211. Official: Inter provide Bastoni injury update as recovery time revealed

Inter confirm Alessandro Bastoni has suffered a left quadriceps strain, which, according to reports in Italy, rules out the Italy international for three weeks.

Inter provided an injury update on their defender Bastoni on Friday after the 27-year-old was forced off in the first half of Wednesday’s Champions League match against Stuttgart.

“Alessandro Bastoni underwent clinical and diagnostic tests this morning at the Humanitas Institute in Rozzano. The tests revealed a strain to his left quadriceps,” Inter said.

According to several sources in Italy, including Sky Sport Italia, Bastoni will be ruled out for at least three weeks.

This leaves Bastoni in doubt for the Supercoppa Italiana Final against Lazio on December 22.

The last Serie A match of the year will be just a few days before, on December 18, when the Nerazzurri will visit strugglers Lecce.

Inter will play seven matches in the next three weeks, including two consecutive matches against Genoa: one in Serie A tomorrow and the following one in the Coppa Italia Round of 16 next Tuesday, both at San Siro.

On Wednesday, December 9, they’ll face Borussia Dortmund away in the Champions League Round 6.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

#1210. Xabi Alonso hits back at former Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher's scathing criticism of his Chelsea centre-backs Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana

Published: 03:35 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 03:35 EST, 27 November 2026

Xabi Alonso concedes Chelsea's defending has been nowhere near good enough – but the Blues boss believes his friend Jamie Carragher was wrong to brand Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana a 'massive problem' in his scathing analysis of the centre-back pairing.

Alonso claimed he had not seen Carragher's critique on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football after their 4-1 home loss to Leeds United.

When told his former Liverpool team-mate had said Colwill and Fofana 'will never work' as defensive partners and that Chelsea 'will never achieve anything' without fixing this problem, Alonso said: 'I must disagree. I disagree with Carra.

'For sure, you can have bad games. We were not good. But I've seen them play well, and I've seen them show good levels.

'This is the goal and the challenge – to be consistent in the performance and to be consistent in the basics and not to drop in certain games when we are facing a tough opponent. I understand it was not good enough.'

Colwill and Fofana were bullied by Dominic Calvert-Lewin of Leeds, as they also were by Sunderland's Brian Brobbey. They will now face Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest on Friday night at a City Ground which will carry an intimidating atmosphere.

Xabi Alonso has hit back at former Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher after he labelled Chelsea's centre backs a massive problem

Alonso and Carragher spent five seasons together as team-mates at Liverpool

Alonso was strong in saying his side can have 'no excuses' for their slipping standards, having conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. 'When you have that feeling like we had on Saturday, it is not good,' the Chelsea manager said.

'We have talked about what we can do better and what we have to do better. There are no excuses not to do better. There are things that we all can do, even if you have a bad day in terms of feeling something you have to do at this level.

'The feeling of the last game is not good, but now it's about looking forward and showing a reaction. There are no excuses. There is no ifs, no buts. Just certainties and things we have to do.

'We can define on the training and the messaging. We need to show that, not just talk. Talk is cheap. It's about performing on the pitch.'

John Terry works for Chelsea's academy part-time, assisting the youngsters coming through at Cobham. Terry is a club legend whose two strengths were defending and leadership.

Asked if he had thought about bringing him on to his staff, Alonso said: 'We have talked because he's been around Cobham many times.

'He's working with the academy. We have people in the staff to prepare for that, and, for sure, the presence of John is always welcome.'

Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana have endured poor starts to the season with Chelsea having already conceded 20 Premier League goals

Pressed further on whether he had worked with the first team, Alonso added: 'This year? Not yet. But he's close to the team.'

Meanwhile, Fofana has apologised to Chelsea for the unauthorised interview he conducted with a YouTuber which sparked a backlash from supporters online.

In it, the centre-back laughed off his penalty miss which condemned the club to their Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool, and revealed how his representatives advised him to honour his lucrative contract, worth £200,000 per week, when he was tempted to quit football amid his injury hell.

Alonso confirmed the club had spoken with Fofana and said: 'He apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, and it was not right, the content. We are here to take things seriously and he said that it's not going to be repeated.'

When asked if Fofana had been fined, Alonso said: 'This is internal things.'

#1209. Arsenal Make Contact to Sign Ivan Fresneda to Replace Ben White

Arsenal have made contact about a January deal to sign a rapid Champions League star as a replacement for Ben White, according to a report.

The Gunners have had a brilliant season so far and sit six points clear at the top of the Premier League, having won nine of their opening 11 games, while they have won three of their five Champions League games and remain undefeated in Europe at this stage too.

But as Mikel Arteta looks to bolster his squad and retain their league title for the first time in their history, it was now emerged that a new addition at full-back is being considered for the January transfer window.

Arsenal have been looking at the addition of a right-sided defender for 2027 for a while now, and with Ben White now 29, it's believed that the position requires future-proofing.

Now, according to Guillermo Rai, the north London side have made contact with the representatives of Sporting CP defender Ivan Fresneda over a potential January switch.

The 22-year-old, who made his debut for the Spain national team in October, has been a regular for the Portuguese side for a number of seasons, has 18 months remaining on his contract in Lisbon, and is someone that Arsenal have been tracking for a while.

The Gunners view the former Valladolid star as a long-term replacement for White, who is out of contract at the Emirates Stadium in 2028, with the option of a further 12 months.

It's unclear how much a deal is likely to cost, but the Spaniard has £69m release clause in his contract. Sporting would likely be willing to accept offers below that value though, considering the length on his deal and clubs interested in his services.

Arsenal's greatest strength at the moment is their defensive solidity, with the physical prowess and technical quality within their backline making them the best in Europe.

But while Fresneda is a solid defender, he is more forward thinking in his style of play, and would provide a greater attacking threat than White or Jurrien Timber.

The youngster would also bring incredible pace to the side, having been recorded as one of the fastest players in the Champions League in the 2025/26 season, and that will certainly help Arteta to take the team to the next level.

Whether the talks being held leads to an actual move happening in January remains to be seen, with a summer move also possible, but it's clear that Arteta has identified Fresneda as the man he wants as the next right-back in his squad.

The Spaniard could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

#1208. Italy cut gap in race for extra Champions League spot

Five wins and two draws for the seven Serie A representatives in Europe helped Italy gain ground in the UEFA coefficient rankings, narrowing the gap to the top two nations, England and Portugal.

Italian clubs went unbeaten in midweek European action. Inter and Como won in the Champions League, while Roma and Napoli drew away to PSG and Manchester City, respectively.

Juventus and Milan won in the Europa League on Thursday, while Atalanta also claimed victory, coming from two goals down to secure a 3-2 away win over Borac in the Conference League.

Italy remain sixth in the UEFA coefficient rankings, but the positive results have helped the country close the gap on the top two nations, England and Portugal.

Italy’s average points total is currently just 686 points below that of second-placed Portugal. However, Portugal have only five teams competing in Europe, compared with Italy’s seven.

Only the two countries with the highest average points totals will earn an extra place in the 2027–28 Champions League.

#1207. Revealed: The Truth Behind Newcastle Interest in Signing Ivan Toney

Newcastle United are looking to seal a number of deals to strengthen their squad in the January transfer window for Matthias Jaissle.

The Magpies have had a mixed start to the season so far, claiming positive results against Tottenham, Liverpool, and Arsenal in the Premier League, while they have suffered heavy defeats to the likes of Leeds, Everton and newly-promoted Coventry City.

The club saw a number of key players depart in the summer, while the players that were brought in were largely unproven at the top level, and the new manager is keen to add more firepower to the team as a result.

In attack, current options William Osula, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, and Yoanne Wissa have combined for just two goals in the Premier League this season, and that has seen the club linked with a move to bring former Brentford star Ivan Toney back to the top-flight.

The England international moved to Saudi Arabia in the summer of 2024 and has been in fine form in the Middle East, and has played under Jaissle while playing for Al-Ahli, scoring 55 goals across two seasons.

His current contract is due to expire in 2028, and there has been speculation that he could look to return to England in the coming transfer window, with a return to St James' Park reportedly on the agenda.

Toney spent three years with Newcastle between 2015 and 2018, but made just four appearances for the club before joining Peterborough United permanently, following several loan spells away.

Reports have suggested that the club could be interested in bringing him back in January, but according to The Athletic, senior club officials have played down that possibility and a deal is not expected to happen. The club are, however, looking at alternative striker options for a January deal, including Dion Dren Baljo.

Newcastle need goals, and Ivan Toney scores goals. If the player is open to a move, and a deal can be done, then it would be a complete no-brainer for Newcastle to pursue it and get it over the line.

Not only is he a goalscoring machine, but Toney also knows the Premier League really well, having scored 36 goals in three seasons with Brentford, before making the move to the Middle East. But in addition to that, he already knows the manager, the style of football, an the way the manager works, which should help him hit the ground running.

Wages could be a problem, but the Saudi connection with the club could make that a bit easier too. For the club not to be confident of getting a deal done suggests they have other things lined up, and fans will be desperate for whoever comes in to make an instant impact, so the board and manager simply cannot afford to get it wrong.

Manchester United are in talks over a move to sign Calvin Bassey from Fulham in January. The 26-year-old has emerged as United's top defensive target for the winter transfer window, as Mauricio Pochettino tries to strengthen his squad.

United are in desperate need to add to their back-line after conceding the most goals (36) across Europe's top five leagues in all competitions this season. They have kept just one clean sheet in 17 matches and that came in the 4-0 rout over Azerbaijani minnows Sabah back in September.

It's a defensive record that must improve if Pochettino wants to have a positive impact at Old Trafford, and work has started on bolstering the back-line in January. According to The Athletic, talks are taking place to understand the conditions for a potential transfer for Fulham defender Bassey, who has impressed in the Premier League for a number of seasons.

The Nigerian was rewarded with the captain's armband at Craven Cottage in the summer and has grown into status since Alvaro Arbeloa's arrival. Indeed, he is Fulham's first-choice centre-back now and the Whites are pushing to extend his contract.

Bassey is an excellent one-v-one defender and is strong at driving with the ball. He would strengthen United's back-line should they decide to bring him to the club in January, though Fulham are determined to keep him.

Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and Brentford's Nathan Collins are among the other Premier League defenders United are interested in. But the Reds are conscious about Branthwaite's injury record and feel they could be priced out of a move for Collins.

Despite United's interest in Bassey, Branthwaite and Collins, the Reds should make Borussia Dortmund's Joane Gadou their priority centre-back target for the January transfer window. The 19-year-old produced a stellar performance for the German side in their 1-1 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday and has been a revelation this season.

Gadou, who joined Dortmund in a £20million deal from Red Bull Salzburg in May, was Dortmund's standout performer at the Emirates Stadium and was unfortunate not to be awarded with the Player of the Match prize, which went to Noni Madueke.

Starting on the right side of a back three, the 6ft 5in wonderkid won eight out of his 10 duels, and made two tackles, one interception, seven clearances and two blocks. He ensured Christos Tzolis had an evening to forget on Arsenal's left.

He is an excellent one-v-one defender, is good at reading the game and has unbelievable athleticism and pace to recover when needed. As well as that, he is strong in the air, winning both of his aerial duels against Arsenal.

Although Gadou impressed from a defensive point-of-view, he was as good, if not better, on the ball. Indeed, the France Under 21s international provided a moment of magic leading to Dortmund's second-half equaliser in north London.

Picking up the ball in his own half, Gadou drove past Tzolis and at least 40 yards up field before picking out a pass, playing a composed ball through to Maximilian Beier, who took one touch and buried a low shot past Kepa Arrizabalaga.

It's an assist that has gone viral on social media, with Dortmund sharing it and getting more than 500,000 views, while others have lauded praise on the 'unbelievable' and 'insane' teenage defender who is catching the eye.

Along with the assist, Gadou progressed the ball on several other occasions. He completed 22 out of his 22 passes, made three accurate passes into the final third and had three progressive passes. In total, Gadou had 50 touches and one shot.

Gadou's profile is unique. Les Parisien described him as "tall, athletic, and not clumsy with the ball at his feet", adding that he is "efficient in both penalty areas." Meanwhile, France Under 17s head coach Jean-Luc Vannuchi said Gadou is a "force of nature", saying that he "combines power and speed", as well as being "interesting with his use of the ball."

He is both "capable of playing short [and] playing long", according to Vannuchi. Yohan Cabaye, the former Newcastle United and Crystal Palace midfielder, highlighted Gadou's efficiency in one-on-one situations and above-average speed.

Flashscore gave Gadou a 8.2/10 rating for his performance against Arsenal - the second highest on the pitch behind Madueke (8.5) - and his progress has not gone unnoticed. BILD have reported that United, Liverpool and Arsenal are monitoring Gadou's progress, with Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain among the others interested.

But Dortmund are not fazed by the attention Gadou is getting, due to the fact he is under contract until 2031 and he has no release clause attached. The Bundesliga outfit are not considering a sale for less than £69m.

Despite that, United should pay what it takes to land Gadou in January. He is a generational talent and they will regret not moving first to sign him. The Frenchman will turn out to be one of the best defenders in world football in the future.

While Bassey, for example, is a more cost-effective option given the fact United won't have to spend more than £30m on him, he is seven years older than Gadou and doesn't have the same potential or even resale value.

Gadou has the talent to become the most expensive defender ever, and for £69m, United would be getting someone that could at least double their value, if not more, should he keep on the same trajectory.

He has made 17 appearances for Dortmund this season and has been a firm fixture in Niko Kovac's first XI. Before someone else does, United need to move fast to land him in January, and he should be their first-choice centre-back target.

Gadou and Leny Yoro could be United's long-term centre-back partnership. Even for now, that is what it would be if the Reds were to land the 2007-born sensation in January, with Harry Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt as back-up.

Man Utd's shocking start to the 2026/27 is record breaking and it has fans worried about relegation, but how many times has that happened in history?

#1205. Enzymatic reactions adapted to make ‘living’ chains of sugars

Yang Ji is in the Department of Pharmacology, School of Medicine, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, and at the Key University Laboratory of Metabolism and Health of Guangdong, Southern University of Science and Technology.

Peng George Wang is in the Department of Pharmacology, School of Medicine, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, and at the Key University Laboratory of Metabolism and Health of Guangdong, Southern University of Science and Technology.

Long chains of sugars known as polysaccharides support many biological functions, from strengthening tissues to modulating cell signalling. Synthesizing these compounds in the laboratory with precise lengths and architectures, which are needed to establish how the structures of polysaccharides affect biological behaviour, has been difficult. Writing in Nature, Yin et al.1 now report an enzyme-based strategy that produces highly uniform polysaccharides and enables chains to restart growth after consuming all of the sugar building blocks in the reaction, once more sugars are added. The authors achieved this control by adjusting how readily an enzyme binds the small sugar molecules that are used to initiate the growth of each chain.

#1204. Wonderkid Confirms Tottenham Deal As Spurs Beat Arsenal To Next Williams-Barnett

Luca Williams-Barnett has finally made the breakthrough that many Tottenham Hotspur fans have been anticipating for years.

The 18-year-old scored and assisted on his full Premier League debut on Saturday, as Spurs beat Ipswich Town 2-0 to move into the top half of the table.

All eyes will now be on Roberto De Zerbi's team selection for the game with Sunderland on Sunday, to see if the teenage star is handed a second successive start in the top flight.

With Savio and Mathys Tel both out injured, the likelihood is that he will be thrown into the starting lineup once more, but De Zerbi may look to ease the pressure on him and take him out of the limelight, particularly away from home in a hostile Stadium of Light atmosphere.

It has taken a while for Spurs to see another young player come out of the academy and really follow in Harry Kane's footsteps and make the grade at the club, with Harry Winks and Oliver Skipp failing to come close to those heights.

Attention will soon turn to who could be next, with Tottenham working hard behind the scenes to ensure progression from the youth ranks is improved.

During last month’s Fan Advisory Board meeting, Spurs confirmed that they had been actively recruiting players under the age of 16, to showcase their commitment to the academy setup.

#1202. Most Disappointing Premier League Players of 2026/27 [Ranked]

It's far too early to make sweeping conclusions about the Premier League season or individual players, although a number of stars at the likes of Manchester United, Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur have certainly had disappointing starts to the new campaign.

All three of these clubs spent big over the summer, in an attempt to rejuvenate them in their pursuit of their respective goals. United were looking to consolidate their place in the top four, Spurs are still striving to be a part of this European-qualifying elite, and City have aspirations of usurping Arsenal as champions​​​​​​. Not all of these objectives are off the table, although all three clubs will be somewhat frustrated with how they've performed, with particular players underwhelming.

However, these aren't the only clubs that have flattered to deceive, with the likes of Chelsea, Aston Villa and Sunderland all enduring difficult campaigns — let down by out-of-form individuals whom they'd expect more from.

With that said, GMS have ranked the top 20 most disappointing Premier League players of the 2026/27 season so far.

Coming in at number 20 is Leeds United's Harry Wilson, who signed from Fulham over the summer on a free transfer. While the lack of a transfer fee means the Yorkshire club can stomach a disappointing campaign from Wilson, it doesn't make his lacklustre performances any less frustrating. After scoring 11 goals and providing eight assists across all competitions for the Cottagers last term, he was viewed as an incredible pick-up for Leeds, yet he's 11 games into his Whites career, and he's yet to get off the mark. Daniel Farke is already preparing to sign an upgrade.

Similarly, Yoane Wissa was expected to kick on and provide value to Newcastle this term after an injury-ridden debut campaign on Tyneside. Netting just once so far this season, the DR Congo international certainly hasn't shown many tangible signs of improvement.

Meanwhile, Crystal Palace signed Axel Disasi in the summer, hoping that he'd help replace Marc Guehi, who left for City in January. The Chelsea loanee has been nothing short of disastrous at Selhurst Park, as the Eagles currently sit rock bottom of the Premier League, having shipped 27 goals — more than anyone else.

Mykhailo Mudryk's fortunes at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium haven't been much better. While expectations were on the floor when Spurs opted to sign him on loan on deadline day, given he'd not played for 18 months due to a drugs ban, he's still managed to be a disappointment. December is upon us, and the Ukrainian has made a solitary appearance for the Lilywhites — a 16-minute cameo off the bench against Nottingham Forest in September.

Dominik Szoboszlai has disappointed for Liverpool, but in a completely different way from all of the above. The Hungarian was the Reds' talisman last season and was expected to ascend to another level as the Merseyside club's definitive best player after the departure of Mohamed Salah. Aside from a handful of wonder strikes, he seems to have taken a step backwards, holding Liverpool back in games with his inability to control the tempo of matches.

Top 20 Most Disappointing Premier League Players 2026/27

Chelsea have had a goalkeeping problem in recent seasons, with Robert Sanchez's antics in between the sticks costing them points on a regular basis. The Blues sought to fix this issue in the summer by signing Emi Martinez, and many believed that this acquisition would prove to be a bargain. It certainly hasn't. The Argentine has disappointed at Stamford Bridge, making a number of uncharacteristic errors already.

Along similar lines, Sunderland thought they'd managed a coup in the transfer market when they landed Kevin Danso late in the window. However, the Austrian certainly hasn't sured the Black Cats' defence up, with his most notable moment being his sending-off against Bournemouth back in October. He now finds himself below the likes of Nordi Mukiele and Luke O'Nein in Regis Le Bris' pecking order.

Savinho is another summer signing who is yet to get going at his new club. The Brazilian was brought in by Roberto De Zerbi at Tottenham to provide the Lilywhites' attack with some stardust. Eyebrows were raised at the £75 million fee, and the winger has done little to silence the sceptics so far. He's scored just one goal and has spent most of the season on the sidelines, injured.

Another player who has hardly featured this season is Jack Grealish. Everton were over the moon when they were able to secure the England international's services for another season in the summer, but three months into the campaign, he's started just three league games, contributed to no goals and has been frozen out due to disciplinary issues.

Speaking of letdowns, Bradley Barcola's start to life at Liverpool has been acutely underwhelming. He's certainly shown glimpses of his ability here and there, but failing to score in your first nine league appearances when you cost in excess of £120 million isn't a good look. There's still ample room for the Frenchman to prove himself, but he's yet to do so in English football.

Top 20 Most Disappointing Premier League Players 2026/27

Several teams could win belated league titles with Man City found guilty over their 115 charges, but Mikel Arteta’s men still wouldn’t get a trophy.

Similarly to Mudryk, the expectations weren't exactly high for Alejandro Garnacho when he completed his summer move, given how recent seasons have panned out for the winger. However, the Argentine has still managed to achieve a bottom-percentile outcome​​​​​​. He's been used sparingly by Unai Emery at Aston Villa, until recent matches, when he hasn't even made the bench.

Omar Marmoush was signed by Spurs alongside Savio from City, and while neither has set the world alight in North London, the Egyptian's start has arguably been more disappointing. While the Brazilian has the excuse of hardly playing due to injury, Marmoush has played plenty of minutes and scored just one goal.

Half of Manchester United's squad could arguably make this list, but many of Mauricio Pochettino's men were coming into this season from a place of low expectation. That cannot be said of Senne Lammens, who was highly rated based on his debut season at Old Trafford, and has since seen his performances decline significantly. A number of high-profile errors have cost United goals and points.

Across Manchester, another goalkeeper is having a dire season. Gianluigi Donnarumma, widely regarded as one of the world's best shot-stoppers, has been off the boil in this department this season, adding to his calamitous work with the ball at his feet.

The Italian's teammate, Marc Guehi, has been equally catastrophic. So dependable last term, the former Crystal Palace captain has seemingly been rocked by Enzo Maresca's less-stable system and has subsequently made an array of mistakes leading to goals.

Top 20 Most Disappointing Premier League Players 2026/27

The numbers show that Bruno Fernandes has still been one of the most creative players in the Premier League this season. The extent to which he's been poor has likely been overblown, but that's not to say he hasn't been extremely disappointing based on the heights he hit last term as Player of the Season. He hasn't been able to carry United's attack in the same way through his playmaking, and that's not to mention some of his questionable antics as the captain of the Red Devils.

Sandro Tonali was one of the summer window's biggest acquisitions, arriving at Tottenham from Newcastle for £100 million. While it's not his fault that he was bought for such a significant sum, he's certainly not justified Spurs' investment with his performances. He's played at a respectable level, but he hasn't looked remotely capable of being the talismanic figure De Zerbi's team needs to lead them towards a Champions League place.

United have obviously been the biggest underperformer this season, and this list unsurprisingly reflects this. Lisandro Martinez comes in at number three, producing several dismal performances that have contributed to the Red Devils conceding 23 goals in 11 matches. He's been all at sea positionally and in possession, whilst his small frame has seen him physically dominated by imposing forwards. Let's not forget he also publicly called out the club's summer signings and the board, despite being a disaster himself.

Youri Tielemans has been even more disappointing than his teammate. The Belgian was expected to finally provide United with a tempo-setting metronome in the middle of the park, but has instead been a liability, with his limited physical attributes leaving the north-west team's defence exposed in transition throughout matches.

Finally, the Premier League's most disappointing player so far in the 2026/27 season has to go to Enzo Fernandez. Acquired for a staggering £125 million, he's been largely diabolical for the Citizens, not translating his excellent form from last season to his new club. Three months in, and it's already clear that Maresca's best midfield doesn't involve the Argentine.

He cannot play alongside Rayan Cherki, as this leaves Elliot Anderson exposed at the base of City's midfield. Thus, Maresca has to play Ayyoub Bouaddi alongside Anderson, forming a double pivot, and Cherki's superior output to Fernandez means the World Cup winner should generally be left on the bench.

Published: 06:38 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 06:46 EST, 27 November 2026

An A-League power couple has quietly split, with both parties engaging lawyers.

Championship-winning goalkeeper Jamie Young and his glamorous lawyer partner Abbey John separated in August 2025 after more than five years together.

Mr Young won the A-League championship in 2022 with now-defunct Melbourne club Western United. During this time, Ms John was a fixture on the sidelines along with their newborn.

The Daily Mail understands the split is acrimonious, with both sides engaging legal representation.

Ms John, 31, and Mr Young, 41, both confirmed their separation to this publication.

The couple were together for five years, before quietly splitting in August last year

Ms John was a fixture on the sidelines along with their newborn when Mr Young was playing for now-defunct Melbourne club Western United

Brisbane-born Ms John met Mr Young in a café in the Queensland capital while he was playing for the Brisbane Roar.

After he was dropped as their first-choice goalkeeper, the couple moved to Melbourne, where he played for United before moving to Melbourne City FC, retiring last year.

Mr Young, who was born in Brisbane and is of Scottish and Sri Lankan descent, also represented England as a youth international.

He was a fan favourite among A-League supporters.

It is understood both Mr Young and Ms John relocated to Brisbane after their split.

Ms John now runs Estates Now, a wills, estate planning and probate firm, but is looking to expand into family law.

Mr Young is a high-performance consultant who mentors young prospective footballers.

#1200. Better Than Araujo: Man Utd Already Know Priority First Signing For Pochettino

Manchester United are in dire need of a new left-back in January. Lisandro Martinez was used in that position for the 2-2 draw at Sporting CP on Wednesday, after Diogo Dalot was dropped following another dismal performance in the 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool.

Luke Shaw is nearing a return to full fitness, however, and is expected to take back that spot soon, after missing the last seven weeks with a muscle problem. Despite that, Shaw has struggled even when available and United should look to upgrade in the transfer window.

According to Sport Witness, United are showing interest in Sporting left-back Maxi Araujo. It's understood the Reds have been monitoring the Uruguay international for a number of months now, and, of course, saw him up close at the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Wednesday.

Araujo has a £67million release clause in his contract, but United could get him for less in January. As well as that, he is believed to be 'very open' about making the move to Old Trafford and has previously expressed his desire to play in the Premier League.

It could be a smart signing, but United should avoid Araujo and instead target someone else. While the 26-year-old did win Sporting's second spot-kick as he was fouled by Senne Lammens and was an attacking threat, he has some big flaws to his game.

Indeed, in the draw against United, Araujo lost possession NINE times, completing just 86 per cent of his passes (38/46) and having one out of four successful dribbles. He didn't make a single accurate pass into the box and completed just one successful cross.

Alongside that, Araujo's defending flattered to deceive. He won just 42 per cent (8/19) of his duels, one tackle and committed three fouls. The ex-Puebla and Toluca man started as a left wing-back and often got caught out with Amad Diallo having joy on that side.

While he can be strong going forward, Araujo does struggle defensively and has proven that on a number of occasions this season. None more so than in the 3-2 defeat to LASK in the Champions League last month, where he could have done better for all three goals. He didn't stop the cross for LASK's first, while both the second and third came down his side.

Considering that and the fact United have conceded the most goals (36) in Europe's top five leagues across all competitions this season, the Reds need a more defensive-minded left-back and Newcastle United's Lewis Hall would be perfect.

The Athletic have reported that United remain interested in Hall, and although it could be difficult for them to persuade Newcastle to sell in January, the Reds need to do all they can to sign him. The England international is one of the best left-sided defenders in the Premier League right now and would be an exceptional addition, even if he is expensive.

Defensively, there are not too many better than Hall about. He produced an impressive performance to keep Lamine Yamal quiet in England's famous 3-2 win against Spain earlier this month, and has been a nemesis for many a right-winger in recent times.

He can attack as well. Indeed, in 113 appearances for Newcastle, Hall has directly contributed to 13 goals. Earlier this season, Hall found the net in a 2-1 win at Hull City and grabbed an assist in a 2-2 draw at home against Bournemouth.

United should go all out to bring Hall to Old Trafford. He should be their first-choice target with Araujo and Antonee Robinson behind. Despite their league position, the Reds should be targeting the best in class - and Hall is just that.

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe heaped praise on the "outstanding" Hall last season, despite leaving him out of the starting line-up to face Arsenal. “Lewis is an outstanding player and you never for any second doubt his qualities and what he can bring to the team," Howe said, when asked the reason behind Dan Burn's inclusion in the team at left-back.

Meanwhile, Pochettino worked with Hall for a brief period at Chelsea and wished him well as he moved to Newcastle. Acknowledging his potential, the Argentine said: “He was unlucky that he could not play [more], but he has a good future and I hope he can settle well there.”

Thomas Tuchel hailed Hall's progress during the recent international break, saying he made a "big impression" on the England team.

The Red Devils must stay locked on their primary left-back target

#1199. Cissè’s goal rate beats Mbappé and Haaland: how Milan’s breakout star compares

Alphadjo Cissè already has 10 goals in his first four months at Milan, and on goals per minute he is ahead of Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland.

As noted by Sky Sport Italia, the 20-year-old’s header against Olympiacos on Thursday took him into double figures for the season. He has six in Serie A and four in the Europa League, from just 15 appearances.

Those numbers are even more impressive given how little he has played. He has started and completed the full 90 minutes only twice, and has played 782 minutes in total. That works out at a goal roughly every 78 minutes. He has also been ruthless in front of goal, converting 40% of his 25 shots.

Across all competitions in Europe, only Raphinha (a goal every 58.8 minutes) and Roma’s Donyell Malen (67.4) have a better rate. Cissè sits ahead of Mbappé (84.7), Haaland (95.7) and Lamine Yamal (111.2).

In Serie A alone, Malen is again the only forward ahead of him. Cissè’s rate of a goal every 74.3 minutes beats Lautaro Martínez (91.5), Francesco Pio Esposito (109.3) and Marcus Thuram (135.5).

He is also in form, having scored in three straight games against Genoa, Frosinone and Olympiacos.

His 10 goals already match Rafael Leão’s total for the whole of last season, which took the Portuguese 1,968 minutes. Cissè has done it in less than half that time.

#1198. Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Liverpool and Brighton & Hove Albion at Anfield.

Liverpool are on a three-game winning run in all competitions, and came from two goals behind in their previous outing in the Champions League on Tuesday, earning an enthralling 4-3 victory over Villarreal. Last weekend, Andoni Iraola’s men also initially fell behind against Brentford in the Premier League, but netted two second-half goals through Daniel Munoz and Alexander Isak to win 2-1 as their opponents finished with nine men.

In his programme notes, Liverpool boss Iraola was excited about the prospect of a second game in a week at home. “As someone who believes every single opportunity we have to play a game at this stadium and in front of our supporters is a privilege, I also feel very passionately that this is a period that we should continue to embrace,” he said.

“It is also a spell in which we will carry on being tested because the quality of the opposition dictates that there is no chance of anything else. Villarreal pushed us all the way in midweek and everything about the way Brighton have played so far this season tells us that it would be foolish to expect anything but the same today.”

Brighton have emerged as one of the surprise packages of the Premier League season thanks to their blistering start. Fabian Hurzeler’s side sit third in the table, having scored a whopping 23 goals in their opening seven games, while conceding just five. On Thursday, Brighton were unexpectedly held to a 0-0 draw by Czech outfit Jablonec, ending a run of six straight victories in all competitions. Nevertheless, they’re unbeaten since their 4-3 league loss to Chelsea back on August 30.

Defender Ferdi Kadioglu believes his team’s energy and fitness has played a huge role in their eye-catching form. “If you want to play how we play, you have to be very fit,” he said. “We were already fit last season, but I think it’s more that now everyone really understands what we need to do to win matches. That’s really clear this season, and everyone is doing it. Everyone is really focused on their task and doing it very well so far.”
